pool.titulo: The GTAs that are still worth playing while you wait for GTA 6 on PC
pool.resumen: I bet GTA 6 doesn't even have a jetpack.
pool.contenido:
Play This Right Now Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.
The big day has been and gone, but you and me? We're locked out in the cold. Grand Theft Auto 6 is enthralling a gazillion console owners across the globe, but those of us loyal to our desktops (or, perhaps, without the means to buy a console to play the thing on) are waiting for its practically certain PC port, may it come sooner rather than later.
But you know what? Who cares! If you want a GTA fix on PC, you've still got plenty of options to choose from. Here are PC Gamer's three biggest criminals to tell you what you should be playing while we wait for Rockstar to get its act together.
Grand Theft Auto 4 Is there any sentence in GTA more iconic than "Cousin, let's go bowling!" Growing up, GTA was a game about rampaging, about stealing tanks, helicopters, and seeing how many cops you could slaughter by holing up in some building site, or making a last stand on the freeway. It was never a game I expected to make me feel something.
But GTA 4 has the best story in the series—a quintessential rags-to-riches narrative that, through Nico's perspective as an immigrant to Liberty City, is the most thorough exploration of the American Dream (arguably, the theme in GTA) that the games have ever managed. It's got that satirical bite, but it's perhaps the first and only time GTA ever properly pulled off those heartbreaking RPG-style choices that genuinely surprise you.
It's a wonderfully paced game which sees Nico ascend the heights of Liberty City's criminal ladder, plus it's got some excellent DLC, which Rockstar used to flesh out other characters in the city. But while its missions still stand up, its silliest moments are often the most memorable, like stumbling out of a bar after getting drunk with your cousin and trying to drive home without killing you both. That, or its wild array of cheats and mods, like the one that makes traffic 9999999% faster .
Grand Theft Auto 5 GTA 5 has had more room to breathe than any other game in the series—13 whole years!—and that sort of overexposure can make it easy to forget just how good this one is.
Intertwining the stories of three protagonists meant there was always a slightly different vibe you could go for—Franklin's fresher, more humble small-time gang origins, Michael's rich suburban life which belies marital issues and a yearning to return to criminal glory, and… well, Trevor. Who you'll dive in to play as, only to discover he's ended up in a dumpster wearing a dress.
Seamlessly switching between each character and feeling like they'd actually continued to live beyond being at the behest of your inputs was rad, especially when it came to the myriad of heists sprinkled across the story that required you to jump between each character and tackle different roles.
While its story isn't the strongest, it more than makes up for that in vibes. Los Santos is a dream to drive through , its radio stations are some of the best the series has seen, and there's always something to stop and do—be it a quick ATM robbery or a chill game of tennis.
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas We are now in a post-GTA 6 world and yet, somehow, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas still feels like the most ambitious game Rockstar ever made. It is the culmination of the GTA 3 saga: the summit of a mountain we all started climbing in 2001, when that one guy told us his hands were all messed up so we better drive (brother).
It is Rockstar operating at the full mastery of its engine and its target platform, and as a result it bristles with little touches and systems that were nowhere to be seen in GTA 3 and Vice City. Want to get jacked? Hit the gym. Want to get hefty? Hit the pizza place. Want to have sex? Download a shady-ass mod.
You've got territory control, skill-training, extensive character customisation, a huge and diverse map, Tom Petty on the soundtrack—there is simply a huge amount of game here, and arranged in such a way that I genuinely think Rockstar still hasn't quite pulled off since. No, being able to get slightly paunchy in RDR2 doesn't count; absolute unit or bust.
With the original version of San Andreas (rather slimily) removed from Steam to prod people towards buying the Definitive Edition, your options are either to pick up the latter or buy the OG trilogy on the Rockstar games store . Frankly, I'd recommend the Definitive Edition. San Andreas is excellent enough to outshine its remaster's deficiencies, and the modernised controls are pretty handy. And hey, we're on PC—there are ways and means to restore what's missing .

pool.titulo: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
pool.resumen: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real."
pool.contenido:
I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood.
I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom.
"A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer."
Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there."
While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day , either.

pool.titulo: The designer of Atari's notorious E.T. likens the deluge of AI games to events that preceded the '80s industry crash: 'There was a glut of crap on the market'
pool.resumen: Despite this, Howard Scott Warshaw thinks AI will be a "super positive thing" for the industry.
pool.contenido:
The emergence of generative AI coding tools has numerous effects on the games industry this year, but the prominent of these is that it's made Steam an absolute nightmare to navigate . Since the summer, Steam (and other storefronts like itch.io) have been inundated with clones and AI slop games , as AI users turn to tools like Claude to output thousands of low-quality titles.
For many of us, this seems like a new problem. But for one veteran game developer, the scenario is all too familiar. Howard Scott Warshaw is the developer of numerous Atari 2600 games including Yars' Revenge and Raiders of the Lost Ark. But perhaps his most famous (or infamous) game is 1982's E.T. the Extra Terrestrial, the notorious tie-in game that was so terrible Atari buried unsold copies of it in the desert .
E.T. has been cited as a contributing factor in the US video game industry crash of 1983—one of many poor-quality 8-bit titles that hollowed out the gaming market in the States. It's here where Warshaw sees a parallel to today's emerging scenario, though he doesn't necessarily believe it will end in the same way.
In a talk he gave at the DevGAMM Lisbon conference last week (via GamesIndustry.biz ) Warshaw remarked upon how AI coding tools have seemed to rapidly sped up iteration times on game development. "People who used to spend weeks, months or years programming something can now do it in days with AI support," he explained.
"So what does this mean in game development? What it means is we're going to see a lot more games produced. You ever hear of the crash of '83 or '84, the big video game crash? They said the problem that happened in the crash, and I think that was true, was there was a glut of crap on the market, because the machine opened up and anybody could just pop a game out, and they did."
Warshaw pointed out that, at the time "good games were still being made" but these games were "way overshadowed by the crap: and that created a real problem in the game industry." He sees a similar situation emerging now thanks to generative AI tools. "AI is going to have the same impact on a larger scale, because on one level, so many more people can now realise and create a video game than ever could before just using AI. And that's okay, but there's going to be a lot of crap, because most games suck. That's just the way it is."
The reason for this, Warshaw says, is that, like all artistic endeavours "there's some things in life that everybody can see themselves doing, and the truth is most people who do it can't do it very well. And what AI is going to do is make that more possible for people who can't do it to do it." Yet while he thinks that most of the games that result from these ideas "aren't going to be very interesting" he also believes that "it's also going to enable the people who really do have some innovative, interesting and solid ideas to realise those, too."
In short, Warshaw believes that AI will provoke a shift away from technology development to a greater focus on game design, which he ultimately believes is "actually going to be a super positive thing for the video game industry." He also said that, despite observing similar warning signs as in 1983, he doesn't "see the prospect of a crash in the video game industry" and instead expects to see a "reorganisation, where we need better filters to figure out a way to get rid of the garbage games".
Warshaw is certainly correct about AI tools resulting in a flood of crap, but I also think he himself overvalues the inherent worth of ideas in terms of what makes a great game. While ideas themselves can be inherently good or bad, no idea emerges from the creative process unscathed. Indeed, a major factor in creating art of any kind is engaging and grappling with that process, learning how to deal with the friction between the image in your head and what ends up on the page, or the canvas, or your scripting program. That mastery only comes through practice and experience. It cannot be outsourced or circumvented.
But that doesn't change the fact that storefronts are currently being overwhelmed with terrible, AI-assisted games, and it's having all manner of knock-on effects. Earlier this month, Valve admitted it is "running behind" on approving Steam games because it has to keep re-reviewing them, and although Valve didn't cite AI as the cause of this, it's an awful coincidence that this has started happening as AI coding tools result in game submissions shooting through the roof.

pool.titulo: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
pool.resumen: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality."
pool.contenido:
It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion.
One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life.
"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."
Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6, Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained.
Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out.
"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world."
This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does.

pool.titulo: In GTA 6, Cars Are Way, Way More Than Just Getaway Wheels
pool.resumen: GTA has always been obsessed with cars, but in GTA 6 your wheels are for more than just getaways - they're your mobile base.
pool.contenido:
The clue's in the name: Grand Theft Auto is a series obsessed with cars. Stealing them, racing them, modding them, escaping the police in them, bopping your head to their iconic radio stations, and sitting in the passenger seat conversing with colourful NPCs as you drive between missions.
But even in this petrolheaded company, GTA 6 stands out.
I'm not talking about the sheer variety of vehicles , from mobility scooters to muscle cars, nor the distinct grunts of its engines and whirr of superchargers, or even its expanded customization that tweaks everything from the upholstery to the transmission. It goes way beyond that: in GTA 6, your car is a mobile base, an extension of your character that sits at the centre of GTA's revamped and reworked systems. Without a car – specifically, without an owned car, rather than one nicked from the side of the street – I'm naked.
First, your car is the only way to manage all the guns you'll need.
In GTA 6, you physically carry weapons rather than hiding them in magically deep pockets. You can only wield two "longarms" – think rifles and shotguns – at a time, one on your back and one in a hand, and realistically you'll only want to carry one at a time because double-parking guns makes the no-nonsense cops twitchy.
Thankfully the trunk of your car can carry extra weapons (sneaking up to cop cars and jimmying the boot can get you a fresh gun in a pinch). Owned vehicles carry all your purchased weapons at once and you can switch them at will. Whenever I'm planning anything remotely violent, such as the lucrative gang hideout robberies, I take my owned vehicle so I'm prepared for anything.
I want to properly invest in my cars. In upgrades, yes, but also in mastering the act of driving them, learning their nuances and quirks. Second, cars hold stashes of pilfered contraband.
Drugs, marked bills, jewellery: anything you steal worth a damn in GTA 6 is stuffed in a bag slung across your shoulder, and selling it through fences is a reliable way to accrue cash. Like with guns, you can only carry as many bags as you have arms. Your car becomes your pack mule, able to stack several stash bags at once so you can steal in sprees, rather than having to sell after every job.
Again, your owned vehicle is better because it'll retain your stash bags indefinitely, and between sessions. You can hit a drug den, head home to sleep, finish a few missions, quit the game, boot it up again hours later and your stash bag will still be safe. Even if you're busted, you should still be able to retrieve your personal wheels from the impound (and you absolutely should: sneaking into impounds is one of GTA 6's most satisfying activities).
Third, and arguably the most important: your car is a mobile wardrobe that can hold five outfits plus extra hats.
That's more crucial than it sounds because of how the police work in GTA 6. When you're clocked as a criminal, cops will have your description, but a new outfit, hat and sunglasses completely covers the scent of sin. You could buy some new clothes, of course, but you'll need a nearby clothes shop and some cash. It's easier and faster to grab some new gear from your trunk and drive off like nothing happened.
These three factors mean that when I have to dump my owned vehicle – changing cars to lose the police, for example – I feel vulnerable. Thankfully, it's easy to get it back by calling Joey in Chapter 1, or via the ScooterBros app, which you unlock later.
All these systems make me want to properly invest in my cars. In upgrades, yes, but also in mastering the act of driving them, learning their nuances and quirks. In GTA 5, Franklin's Bravado Buffalo S was just another vehicle to me, and I was constantly swapping between stolen cars to get from A to B, each handling differently. In GTA 6, I know exactly how much throttle Jason's Ganado pickup can take before it tailslides, and exactly the right angle for skidding around swampy corners without wrapping around a tendrilled tree.
And I take more care when weaving through traffic because crashing in GTA 6 peels off fenders and crumples bumpers faster than ever.
The Official GTA 6 Guide, Only on IGN Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .
I'm deep into Chapter 2, but (mild spoiler alert!) I haven't even begun registering and storing new cars in garages. I've stolen and sold plenty – another new feature in GTA 6 – and will steal and sell plenty more. No doubt GTA 6's preoccupation with vehicles will continue, and I can't wait to see how cars change as the game unfolds.
If Red Dead Redemption 2 is the horse game, shrunken bollocks and all, then GTA 6 is without doubt the car game.

pool.titulo: Nintendo Knocks $20 off Physical Switch 2 Copies of Donkey Kong Bananza for Black Friday
pool.resumen: Physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza have received a $20 discount in Nintendo's Black Friday sale, bringing its price down to $49.99.
pool.contenido:
Nintendo is officially joining PlayStation and Xbox in launching its own official Black Friday sale for this year. Alongside a very welcome Switch 2 console deal, the sale is also stacked with plenty of physical game deals for the OG Switch and Switch 2. One of our favorite finds for the latter console is Donkey Kong Bananza , which has received a $20 discount that's brought its price down to $49.99.
We've never seen the price for this game drop this low before, which certainly makes the deal a highlight among Nintendo's Black Friday sale selection.
If you've been saving a spot for it in your Switch 2 library, now is a great time to buy. We certainly think the game is worth it, as not only did it earn a 10/10 review score but it's also among our 100 best Nintendo Games of all time and was our favorite Nintendo game of last year .
Donkey Kong Bananza's review featured some mighty high praise from IGN's Logan Plant, who called it "a truly groundbreaking 3D platformer".
This is all thanks to "satisfying movement, powerful abilities, impressive destructible environments, and clever challenges," which ultimately earned it the title of "Masterpiece". It certainly sounds like a must-play if you've got a Switch 2, and what better time to grab it than when it's $20 off?
While Donkey Kong Bananza is easily one of our top deals out of Nintendo's Black Friday sale this year, it's not the only one available. Check out our full breakdown of the sale here to see what other game deals have caught our eye, alongside discounts on hardware and accessories.
As mentioned before, there's also a surprise Switch 2 console deal available at the moment, which is a joy to see after recent price hikes .
The sale runs until November 29 this year, so be quick to grab your favorite deals while they're still in stock.

pool.titulo: Nintendo's 2026 Black Friday Sale is Officially Live
pool.resumen: Nintendo's official Black Friday sale is now live and includes a rare Switch 2 bundle discount, up to 50% off Switch 2 games, MicroSD Express cards, and more. Here's where to find all the top discounts to ensure you're saving as much as you can.
pool.contenido:
Nintendo's official Black Friday 2026 sale is now live across all major retailers . From Nov. 22-29, fans can score up to 50% off a slew of Switch 2 games, some top discounts on memory cards, and the first-ever official Switch 2 Black Friday deal .
That's right, we're actually getting a decent console deal during the Black Friday sales (since both PlayStation and Xbox have gone absent in this regard).
Nintendo Black Friday Sale: Quick Retailer Guide Live at Amazon Live at Target Live at Walmart Live at Best Buy Originally priced at $549.99, including Mario Kart World and a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, this Switch 2 bundle would usually save buyers around $38. But now, with the Black Friday discount applied, savings are closer to $88 in total .
That's not all, however, as there are also a slew of incredible Switch 2 games discounted in the sale. I'll include my absolute top picks just below.
Notably, the third party deals are considerably better than the Switch 2 first party games. Donkey Kong Bananza and Kirby Air Riders are standouts from Nintendo's lineup of games, but falls a little short for recent titles that fans might have been looking out for, like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, Star Fox, and more.
Nevertheless, there's still plenty of great third-party game deals to consider . That includes Resident Evil Requiem for $39.99, and Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, for $59.99. That's just the tip of the iceberg, however, as there's so many good offers that it's hard to just list off everything on sale.
It's especially good as most of these games have been released (or re-released on Switch 2) in 2026. So, it's all new games you're getting a pretty reasonable discount on.
Digital Switch 2 Game Deals On the digital side of things , you can save a little on very recent releases, including the phenomenal The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .
It’s only $5 off, but it just came out. Honestly, it’s the best-looking game Nintendo has ever released, and the 1998-era puzzle design holds up impossibly well . I loved every second of that game, and I look forward to replaying it in a year or so.
Samsung Nintendo Switch Memory Cards on Sale for Black Friday One of the most welcome deals for new Switch 2 owners is on memory ! The Switch 2 only comes with 256GB of onboard storage and it will run out faster than you think. If you have a standard MicroSD card from your previous Switch, it won't work on the Switch 2.
Although the two might look similar, the MicroSD Express card is much faster than its predecessor. The Samsung P9 model boasts transfer speeds of up to 800MB/s.
So, it's good that we've found some fresh offers on Switch 2 memory cards in the Black Friday sale.
Amazon has dropped the price of the highly rated Samsung P9 256GB Micro SDXC Express Card to $44.99 with free shipping. This is a slight $3 price drop from earlier this month and the lowest price I've seen in a while.
The 512GB model is also on sale for $99.99. Are these the lowest prices ever ? No. Are there cheaper memory cards out there? Yes . But if you're looking for a memory card that we've personally tested and recommend , you won't find a better deal right now.
Quite a few games have now been released for the Switch 2 and some of them require an enormous amount of space. Final Fantasy 14 is the most gigabyte-hungry game to date, requiring about 117GB all by itself. That game alone takes up half of the Switch 2's internal storage capacity.
Other plus-sized games include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade (90GB), Split Fiction (70GB), Cyberpunk 2077 (60GB), and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (44GB).
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time tops out at about 27GB. Nowadays it's completely possible to download just three or four games and find yourself completely out of onboard storage.
Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27? Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before what I like to call "Black Friday proper."
Having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a Switch deal hits (like it is on November 22), it usually sticks for the rest of the sale. That means the prices you see now on consoles, games, and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to December. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer.
These offers are reliable, worthwhile, and unlikely to get any better. Grab the games and hardware you’ve had your eye on, there’s no risk of Black Friday regret, only the satisfaction of finally getting exactly what you wanted at a price that makes sense.
Are you planning to pick up anything in Nintendo's Black Friday sale? Let us know in the comments, and stick around with IGN as we continue to update you daily on the best Black Friday deals for 2026.

pool.titulo: I've never known a moment like this in video games
pool.resumen:
It was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch day in a kind of stun-lock. As far as video games editorial goes - which is not that far, in fairness; prepare for an over-flattering analogy - the effect was roughly the equivalent of Tom Hanks' experience, as his John H. Miller first set foot on Omaha beach. Tweets and reels whistled overhead, news leads stung the ears, exploding search terms blew apart some poor guides team ally on one side, while new discoveries in the early game - made by the millions and millions of launch-day players all picking it apart at once - appeared by surprise like some flanking ambush on the other.

pool.titulo: "Diez veces más difícil que hacer Star Wars": el responsable de los efectos de George Lucas sudó tinta para que Clint Eastwood volara y el truco acabó premiado por la Academia
pool.resumen:
Esta semana mi compañero Marcos Yasif me ha pasado un artículo de /Film donde una de esas historias de rodaje que me alegran el día. En el documental sobre la producción de Firefox, el arma definitiva (Firefox, 1982), el director Clint Eastwood se quejaba de un problema que lo tenía frito: cada vez que componían el avión sobre el cielo o sobre la nieve del Ártico, el recorte dejaba una línea negra alrededor del aparato. En el espacio eso no pasa, porque el negro se la come. Para arreglarlo, Eastwood fichó a John Dykstra , que había ganado el Oscar por los efectos de la primera peli de la saga Star Wars en 1977.
Firefox no está entre las mejores pelis de Eastwood ni entre las más famosas, pero a mí me gusta mucho, y luego os cuento por qué. El caso es que antes de revolucionar el western o cruzar los puentes de Madison más románticos, el bueno de Clint estaba obsesionado con ganarle la guerra Fría a los soviético, tan malos ellos a principios de los 80. Así que se la jugó con una peli de ciencia ficción : costó unos 21 millones de dólares, mucho más que cualquier peli que hubiera hecho antes, y lo metía de lleno en el cine de efectos especiales, un terreno que no era el suyo.

Según los últimos datos de Circana , el gasto de los estadounidenses en XBOX Series X|S aumentó un 42% en octubre de 2026 respecto al mismo mes de 2025. Sin embargo, hay un detalle importante detrás de este crecimiento: las unidades vendidas aumentaron un 10% , mientras que el precio medio de las consolas se incrementó un 29% a causa de las subidas del coste. La realidad es que Microsoft vendió más consolas el mes pasado que en octubre de 2025, aunque buena parte del gasto se explica porque los consumidores pagaron más por cada Series X|S.

La frase es tan bonita que circula por ahí como si fuera suya, pero no pertenece al actor. Lo que sí hizo Bridges fue reflexionar sobre la idea de que la peli que acabas rodando es como la piel que una serpiente deja en el suelo y que tú recoges para hacerte una cinta de sombrero, mientras que rodarla es la serpiente misma .
Y ahí entra para él quedarse charlando con los compañeros al acabar la jornada o dejar que otro actor te afecte de verdad, algo que él ve como un lugar espiritual. Me parece una respuesta muy suya, y bastante más de vaquero zen . Los monjes dedican incontables horas a dibujar el mandala, luego lo barren y llevar la arena a un río. El mandala no importa, pero crear el mandala sí . ¿Y qué tiene esto que ver con Tron y la ciencia ficción?

First there was 1995’s Bad Boys , the Will Smith and Martin Lawrence buddy-cop film that became a popular franchise. He closed out the decade with the genre-defining end-of-the-world disaster film Armageddon . And in between those two, he gave us a tightly crafted thriller that is currently free to stream (with ads) on Pluto TV.

pool.titulo: This '90s-inspired horror game has one of the coolest post-apocalyptic worlds I've ever seen
pool.resumen: Plus you can experience it all from the comfort of your campervan.
pool.contenido:
I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical.
You do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo , although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well.
This isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best.
But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left.
The dev, Painted Black Games, says it took inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for The Road of Dust and Sorrow, and while I haven't come across anything particularly traumatic in a Silent Hill sense yet (although I wouldn't be surprised to see that here) I can see the through line to Resident Evil.
The action is smooth, accurate, and rewarding—which surprised me as I usually don't vibe with 2D gunplay, sometimes the controls are too finicky, but it certainly works here. Head-shotting the zombies is incredibly satisfying, as is kicking them to the floor and beating them with a baseball bat.
Then there are the puzzles. I didn't come across too many, but the ones I did find were very rewarding. It's not rocket science, but the solutions aren't always obvious either. They are, however, very intuitive; you can do a lot with a little, something I very much appreciate.
But my favourite aspect of The Road of Dust and Sorrow has to be just how cool this post-apocalyptic world is. Maybe it's the pixel art, but it manages to look dilapidated and creepy while also being oddly pretty to look at. I was searching an abandoned warehouse full of zombies and rotting cargo while thinking to myself that with a bit of elbow grease this place could really scrub up.
If you want pretty and cosy, though, the campervan is where it's at. I didn't spend as much time as I would have liked to there, but it managed to feel like a real home—the only safe place left in this world.

pool.titulo: Former Rockstar environment artist breaks silence: GTA 6 is 'generally stunning,' but Red Dead 2 might have had better rivers
pool.resumen: "I want to celebrate this world that I spent literal years working on."
pool.contenido:
David O'Reilly, an environment artist who worked at Rockstar for 12 years on games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Grand Theft Auto 5, and the just-released GTA 6, recently started a YouTube channel called Game World Art where he explores videogame environments. For the last year and a half or so, he's chatted about those games and others from his point of view, sharing tidbits about the tech involved in making them—and now that GTA 6 is out, he's showing off his work and offering some impressions.
"To set expectations, this is not a Rockstar insider-type channel, it's not telling you exactly how Rockstar makes their worlds, this is more about seeing these kinds of open world games—and this one in particular—through my eyes and my perspective as an environment artist," he said in the video.
In his impressions video, he cruises around for a while and talks about his changing relationship to Rockstar games. Given that putting them together was literally his day job, he couldn't enjoy games like RDR 2 and GTA 5 "to anywhere near the extent" that can enjoy GTA 6—since he left the studio in 2023, he's got some distance from the final game. That doesn't mean he's turning the analytical part of his brain off entirely, though, as he stopped here and there to critique the world he saw.
He called the game's art "generally stunning" and "almost flawless," saying it was visually better than Crimson Desert, which was hamstrung by a "slight jankiness." But he also said he preferred RDR 2's rivers, which he worked on extensively to the point that it became a specialty. If you think he's being persnickety, he did note that he's "obsessed with rivers," and has argued in a previous video that Crimson Desert's rivers "just clinch it" over Red Dead's. Hopefully we can get a definitive river tier list from O'Reilly soon to settle matters on a broader scale.
Still, he had almost exclusively positive things to say, and was careful to note that it's hard for any one artist to take credit for anything on a game as huge in scope as a Rockstar open world heist-'em-up. Ultimately, it seems like he's mostly pleased to see his and his friends' work finally out in the open: "I want to celebrate this world that I spent literal years working on. And I have plenty of friends who are still at Rockstar who have worked on this for a long time, and I couldn't be more pleased for you all."

pool.titulo: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
pool.resumen: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.
pool.contenido:
Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.
As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval. Stoic, nonchalant, calm, composed, resigned; whatever you want to call one of GTA 6's new protagonists, Rockstar says it carefully crafted his already iconic demeanor by pulling from a Steve McQueen classic and real-life veterans.
The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid . Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway.
"Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."
He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers ) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks.
"These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."
Jason is the talk of Vice City and has been for some time. As Rockstar shared more details about its seemingly shy lead ahead of GTA 6's launch, some fans began to wonder if he could be the franchise's first-ever neurodivergent protagonist . In addition to his personality, Humphries described Jason as "wired differently" during a recent interview with Love magazine.
While Jason steals more than just wads of cash in Vice City, his partner in crime has proven to be just as impactful. Game writer Michael Wiafe said looking into the kind of criminal activity known to make headlines in Florida was one of the first things the team did when creating both Jason and Lucia. For Rockstar, it wasn't just about creating true-to-life criminals; it was about creating fully realized human beings.
"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn’t stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What’s important is how they resonate, no matter where you’re experiencing the game in the world."
Between the chaos of robbing gas stations and drug dealers and getting into high-speed car chases, Jason and Lucia can become quite the power couple. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern said to Destructoid, "You really want them to make it." The quiet moments where the duo scrolls through social media in their bed or drives the other one to work can be just as important as the action set pieces. Gauvey-Kern added, "Those need to hit too, and you need to connect with how the characters are feeling in those moments."
Although GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S three days ago, Leonida is packed with enough things to do to keep players playing for months. While we wait to see what's next for Rockstar, you can check out IGN's 10/10 review . You can also read about how the developers made every NPC feel like real people you could run into on the street .

pool.titulo: Forget the Lighthouse, GTA 6’s Best Minigame Is a Full-Blown Zombie Shooter That Will Take You Hours To Beat
pool.resumen: Yes, we know you're all playing GTA 6, but don't forget to check out Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, the certified banger on Jason's JoySystem console.
pool.contenido:
To say I was up until midnight last night with GTA 6 is technically correct, but not the full picture. What I was actually doing was headshotting undead nightmares in Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, a moreish isometric twin-stick shooter that lives inside Jason's PS5-alike JoySystem.
You play it briefly with Cal during the story, and it impressed me enough to want to beat it fully. After nearly four hours, I still haven't.
It's clearly inspired by the Sony-published Dead Nation from 2010, but it mashes the zombie slaying with a roguelike deckbuilder. Every time an enemy squelches, their blood splattering the pavement, you gain XP, and at each new level you pick a card to adjust your build. Basic cards boost movement speed, fire rate, damage or critical hit chance, but rarer cards transform your tactics, such as one that doubles your damage given and received.
Your goal is to collect six gears strewn around a deceptively large map and leave via a rooftop chopper. You'll die a lot, but on each run you'll learn a little more about the world's layout and discover new cards to experiment with.
The satisfaction of Street Trash 3 is in crafting a build on the fly from the cards you're dealt, and in feeling your power spiral. You're constantly levelling up and that escalation, the way your build rapidly grows and branches depending on what you find, reminds me a lot of Vampire Survivors . Like that game, it's most fun when you lean into a specific skill: the closest I've come to victory was when I swapped my pistol for a micro-SMG, buffing and buffing my fire rate until the bullets streamed like a deadly snake.
I also got deep on a run boosting my speed and stamina so I could infinitely sprint from groups of enemies, and another where – inspired by a detailed Reddit thread discussing the best builds – I found a card that improved my critical chance by 50% while standing still. When combined with other critical hit cards, I could basically stand in the same spot and mow down everything down around me, painting a gruesome circle of guts.
There is so much craft that most players simply won't see, so many developer hours spent creating missable moments of delight. It is ludicrous that something as meaty and polished as Street Trash 3 exists inside another video game – and even more ludicrous that it's one of three games you can play on Jason's console (Rockstar told Kotaku that "an internal dev team within the dev team" makes these games).
But, like in real life, not every game available for the JoySystem is a banger. Of the three games on Jason’s hard drive, Time Jackers Rewind is the most forgettable. It's a stylish top-down shooter that plays a bit like a slower, sci-fi, less-good Hotline Miami . I appreciate how its checkpoints are tantalizingly spread far enough that you can't just sprint between them, close enough that after every death I was sure I was seconds away. Sadly its best weapon, a concussive shotgun that rumbles your controller, runs out of ammo after just a few seconds, and it's tricky to see enemies among all the on-screen effects.
Tenenbrae Lux is the third, a joke about auteurs stretched into an entire puzzle game. The developer is Johannes Zuch, a clear play on The Witness developer Jonathan Blow (Zuch/Suck, get it?), and his name is listed 38 times during the end credits, including as "architect as perception" and "left stick sensitivity tension consultant". This, surely, is a send-up of Hideo Kajima popping up multiple times in his own credits. The looping stairway in its central puzzle evokes Kojima's P.T. but if you squint you can also see riffs on Alan Wake, Dear Esther, and Robert Eggers’ black-and-white 2019 film The Lighthouse.
As a puzzler, it's intriguing. I say intriguing rather than fun because I can't say I really enjoyed it. The narrator's dialogue is deliberately grandiloquent and recondite ("Hark! An unearthly sound beckons. Like the sirens call, I am fated to find its source"), and the central puzzle is mind-bendingly complicated. Without completley spoiling it, you must loop through a series of rooms in a bunker and spot anomalies, cross-reference them with other clues to assign them a number, and then arrange those numbers in chronological order using a calendar in each room.
Rewarding when you've solved it, for sure, but a pain when you're trying.
The whole thing takes a couple of hours to complete, less if you look up the strategy guides than now exist across the internet (although note that the bunker puzzle is different for each player). And so if you want to beat all of the games on Jason's console, then, you'll need roughly five hours at the very least. That's a pretty impressive amount of game that's not Grand Theft Auto 6 in your copy of Grand Theft Auto 6.
What I love most about these three games is that they are entirely optional, like the majority of GTA 6. There is so much craft that most players simply won't see, so many developer hours spent creating missable moments of delight, so many systems I haven't yet engaged with. It speaks to both Rockstar's budget and its confidence, and as a player it's comforting to know that pretty much wherever I turn I'll find something hand-crafted and surprising. No matter how much time I put in, I couldn't possibly see everything.
What I can do, though, is see everything in Street Trash 3: Dezombifier. Back in I wade, for one more run.

pool.titulo: American Psycho Remake From Director Luca Guadagnino No Longer Happening
pool.resumen: Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.
pool.contenido:
Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.
The Challengers and Call Me by Your Name movie maker delivered the disappointing news when asked for an update on Deadline's Crew Call podcast. He admitted the script for the project that he read, which was penned by the writer behind The Bourne Ultimatum and Side Effects, was "fantastic" but not something he can continue working on.
"American Psycho, which is a fantastic script from Scott Z. Burns, unfortunately, is not happening for me, as we speak," Guadagnino said.
Guadagnino has more than proven himself as a name capable of handling the weight of a property on the level of American Psycho, which is exactly why movie fans were so excited to hear he could be attached to the project in 2024. Although fans have referred to what would have become his slice into the well-established movie universe as a 'remake,' at the time of its announcement, Lionsgate teased that the project would have been more of an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho novel, rather than a remake of Christian Bale's 2000 movie .
Updates on Guadagnino's American Psycho have been few and far between in the years since its announcement, though. Elvis star Austin Butler was once in the running for the role of Patrick Bateman, as was Euphoria's Jacob Elordi. It was reported in October 2025 that the film would not gender-swap its lead role .
Bale eventually went on to comment on Guadagnino's reimagining and another actor bringing his iconic character to the big screen. He said "all the best to 'em" just earlier this year, adding, "I like brave people."
The director didn't explain why his version of American Psycho won't be moving forward, just that it's "not happening for me." While that means any version of American Psycho won't be coming to movies anytime soon, it's unclear if Lionsgate has completely closed the door on Patrick Bateman. With Burns' script finished, there's always the chance a different filmmaker could take the reins.
For now, though, it's best to assume the American Psycho remake/adaptation is well and truly dead. In the meantime, Guadagnino is gearing up for the release of his Sam Altman biopic, Artificial . The film is gearing up for a limited premiere Christmas 2026 before getting a wider release January 8, 2027.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 needed a dedicated team to make sure all its different body types could share animations: 'It was a huge team effort'
pool.resumen: Making sure your animations don't break while you're cultivating mass.
pool.contenido:
We don't know precisely how big GTA 6's "big boy" budget was, but let's put aside the alarming excess of contemporary mass-consumption entertainment for a moment and talk about the real big boy: bulked up Jason.
While GTA 6's body morphing might not go quite as far (in terms of waistband measurements) as its predecessor San Andreas—or even a game like Fable 2—it does boast extensive variety of different body shapes among its cast, and making that work at such a high level of visual fidelity took an entire dedicated team.
In an interview with IGN , Rockstar vice president of animation Mark Tennant said it was an early decision in development to "push the variation in character sizes and body types … This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat."
It also took eschewing a "traditional approach" in favor of "new techniques," the sort I imagine you can only implement at Rockstar levels of budget and manpower. "We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams," said Tennant. "All these aspects needed to come together to make it work, so it was a huge team effort."
In the same IGN piece, senior technical art director Valmor Garcia said the ultimate goal was to ensure each character had "singular awareness and visual identities," which included giving them unique faces and anatomy (the six-figure animation count is part of that too, I imagine). All the blood, sweat, and so on seem to be paying off given the game's absolutely massive launch , but Saints Row 3 is still the only crime sandbox that lets me replace all my character's dialog with meaningless zombie grunts , so it's impossible to say which is better.

pool.titulo: New Dota 2 patch tries to help games end faster, adds an item that summons super creeps in every lane at once
pool.resumen: It's awfully reminiscent of ideas you can find in other, more fast-paced MOBAs.
pool.contenido:
The longest game of Dota I've played was comfortably past the 70-minute mark. Matches that gloriously long-winded can be fun in small doses, but they can also be exhausting and infuriating—this is Dota we're talking about, after all. The latest patch to rearrange the venerable MOBA, 7.42, is finally here , and it's got tons of changes that might just prevent your games from going feature length.
The most exciting of these, for my money, is the Greater Horn of Battle: a guaranteed drop from the Tormentor neutral monster that summons a wave of super creeps in all your team's lanes (the patch notes refer to them as the more powerful mega creeps, but players have noted the stats don't match up that way). If you've played League of Legends or Deadlock, it fills a niche similar to the Rift Herald or Deadlock's Unstable Rifts—an objective you can complete in the earlier stages of a game to push lane(s) hard.
It's an ability that, if timed correctly, could force the other team to scramble to protect each lane or risk losing lots of ground. And it's not the only change with the potential to speed up matches.
Base hero health has gone up from 120 to 200, with the caveat that strength now gives less health per point, meaning that heroes will be sturdier early on but slightly squishier later. The Glyph of Fortification, a teamwide spell that makes buildings invulnerable, no longer resets its cooldown when certain buildings go down. Heroes also now gain experience passively, even when dead, meaning that you never completely stop growing stronger as the match progresses.
It will probably take some time to see if this actually meaningfully reduces match times or if these changes even stick around for long, but personally, anything that makes Dota a little bit speedier has the potential to reignite my passion for the game. Whenever I dip in these days, it's to play the fastest mode possible—Turbo, which accelerates every aspect of play and gives you oodles of gold just for existing—but it's so different from the traditional Dota setup that it may as well be a new game.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect
pool.resumen: Didn't you hear? You can't even steal cars anymore.
pool.contenido:
If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.
It starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon. A greenscreened science communicator then appears, rubs their forehead, and shows us a video of a ship disappearing over the horizon. Checkmate.
It's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos. Now you're enrolled in a never ending lesson plan which features such insights as 'an all-meat diet is not good for you,' 'the moon landing was real,' and 'hating women is not in fact based .'
The total effect of this is that the most ignorant and dishonest quacks and provocateurs get to set the level of discourse, and instead of investigating new metaphorical horizons in topics that interest you, you wind up watching people debate the existence of the actual horizon.
Which brings me to Grand Theft Auto 6. Despite making $3.79 billion on its launch day, it's easy to stumble across confident social media claims that it's a total flop and everyone's going to refund it. According to popular X posts, GTA 6 doesn't even let you steal cars anymore, and there are hundreds of Metacritic user reviewers insisting that it's far-left propaganda rather than the mass-market entertainment product it obviously is.
It's the videogame discourse version of flat eartherism. The millions of people playing GTA 6 do not think it is a "cuck simulator" because you can buy a woman flowers, but it's hard not to react to the few dorks making that claim, even though focusing on debunking them severely limits the depth of the conversations we can then have about the game. Good luck discussing your feelings if you dislike GTA 6 for normal reasons!
Over the past few days, I've entertained sparks of hope that GTA 6 could be the flashpoint that brings us out of this era of videogame discourse. The millions of people playing it and not reacting like buffoons are surely irrefutable evidence that culture war dunces don't represent the masses.
But then again, we're still pointing at videos of ships going over the horizon to prove that the earth isn't flat.

pool.titulo: Which GTA 6 radio station is your favourite so far?
pool.resumen: The music of Leonida is so damn good.
pool.contenido:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out in the hands of console players for a few days now, and a few of us at PC Gamer have been dusting off our PlayStations and Xboxes to dive into Leonida as we eagerly anticipate its eventual (but yet unannounced) PC release next year potentially.
I've been gaming it up myself and, as is always the case with GTA, I am absolutely loving driving around. Flying down the highway, exploring all the alleyways and retail areas, and taking out to the waters on a boat or jetski. All of it, of course, to the soundtrack of GTA 6's various radio stations.
There are a huge number of stations in this game—19 of them, to be exact—with a ton of excellently-curated songs lingering within and famous cameo hosts. Usually I find myself just picking one station and sticking to it, but with GTA 6? I've been cycling between quite a few, each one offering something a little bit different.
Four stations have been grabbing most of my attention though. Pop station Flash FM has easily gained the most airtime in my playthrough so far. Am I listening to Ariana Grande in my everyday life? No. But am I bombing it down the highway while singing Break Free to myself every time it comes on? I absolutely am.
But I've also been peppering in a ton of 80s station Vice City FM. I mean, c'mon, you've got Weird Al Yankovic as a co-host, first of all. But you've also got straight up bangers like Lionel Richie's All Night Long, Simply Red's Money's Too Tight (To Mention), and Billy Ocean's Loverboy.
There's also Emotion 98.3, the radio station dedicated to songs about love (both being in love and being heartbroken, of course) and yes, I have stayed in the car waiting to hear Phil Collins' excellent drumming in In The Air Tonight. And finally, because I am a raging emo at heart, I've obviously had to whack on a bunch of The Chamber 106.6. Tool, System of a Down, and Metallica? Count me in.
But what about you? If any of you PC gamers are partaking on console, is only one radio station catching your attention, or have you found yourself channel hopping just like me? Or is there somehow not a single station that's caught your fancy, instead finding the podcasts a more entertaining use of your listening time? Be sure to drop a comment and let me know.

pool.titulo: GTA 6's massive casino and sick go-kart track are currently closed, but I'm hoping we can trust those 'coming soon' signs 🙏
pool.resumen: And not just for GTA 6 Online, right? Right?
pool.contenido:
I'd just stolen my very first airplane in GTA 6 and was happily cruising over the city when I looked out my window and saw an enormous purple building. I banked, slowed down, and flew a bit closer to read the huge sign on the roof.
VICE CITY CASINO
Oh, hell yes. I was so excited to throw my carefully accumulated three hundred dollars away on poker and slots that I immediately attempted my very first landing. After the explosion and my miraculous resurrection, I rushed back to the casino and crashed again, this time with my body into the locked front doors.
The casino in GTA 6 is closed. Trust me, I tried every door, and the only one that opened was a utility closet.
I was early into my playthrough, still in Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 story missions , so I thought maybe there'll be some mission that unlocks the casino so I can play some poker, try my luck at the slots, and maybe bet on the also-closed dog track—I assume it's a dog track because I've seen dogs in GTA 6, but no horses—that's right next door to the casino.
Nope! I'm now 100% done with the main story and that casino is still closed. And that's not the only business in GTA 6 that isn't open for business. Not even a half-mile away from the casino there's a go-cart track called Hot Skidz sporting a huge "Coming Soon" sign. I saw that early in my game as well, and checked back later. Still closed. I also found a second, smaller casino. Also closed.
What a letdown. I managed to get my motorcycle onto the go-cart track, and as I drove glumly around it, alone, having no fun, I perked up a bit. Maybe this just gives me something to look forward to. A hint of more singleplayer content that'll be coming to GTA 6 next year. Hopefully next year.
There's already a lot of seemingly unfinished stuff in GTA 6, partial systems that could be added to and completed, like:
I can throw a frisbee but no one will catch it—not even dogs—or throw it back I can go to a tennis court, pick up a tennis racket and tennis ball, and hit the ball with the racket, but I can't actually play tennis Speaking of dogs, who would put so many dogs in a game and not let me have my own dog? There's a baseball bat and baseballs, but I can't play baseball The dog thing is madness. Gotta let us have dogs at some point There are so many cool houses but I can only live in the one currently assigned to me by the story There are hotels everywhere but I can't rent a room You can play eight-ball pool but not nine-ball? Pure insanity, even moreso than the dog decision There's tons of construction sites, so many it can't just be satire about America's horrible infrastructure, they've gotta at least build a new few things for us to play with Like, no offense to the snake, but I want a damn dog I felt better after that, but as I went back to stare at that huge, closed casino—which is all lit up at night like it's actually open, even though it is not open, and I know this because I rechecked all the doors—I remembered how the casino in GTA 5 worked. It came to the game post launch, but only as part of GTA Online. It never opened in singleplayer.
But surely, why include the building at all in GTA 6 singleplayer if it wasn't also going to be in singleplayer? They wouldn't do that to us, would they? They wouldn't open it in GTA 6 Online and not open it in GTA 6 singleplayer.
That would be like putting dozens of dogs in a game and not letting us have our own dog. Madness.

pool.titulo: Scott Lynch, author of The Lies of Locke Lamora, has 1,493 hours in Star Wars: Rebellion and 1,564 in BattleTech: 'If J.R.R. Tolkien had had a Steam account, his numbers would be pretty embarrassing too'
pool.resumen: The fantasy novelist guides us through the games on his PC.
pool.contenido:
Disk Cleanup Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"
Playing on school computers has been a rite of passage for many young PC gamers, whether through dedicated edutainment titles or rogue installations by chancing pupils. But fantasy novelist Scott Lynch went one step further: he took the school computers home.
"My mother worked for our school district, so I'd occasionally have the chance to sneak into the computer lab, or we would borrow and Apple II over the summer," Lynch says. "When we did that, I borrowed Infocom games … text-only adventure games from the '80s like Zork, Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Planetfall, A Mind Forever voyaging. I was really into those when I was about 12."
Text-based adventures would eventually become a defining feature of Lynch's life, albeit in a different format. His debut novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora , was published in 2006, charting the schemes and adventures of a group of master con artists called The Gentleman Bastards. Two further novels in The Gentleman Bastard Sequence have since followed: 2007's Red Seas Under Red Skies , and 2013's The Republic of Thieves
Lynch currently working on a novella in the same world called More Than Fools Fill Graves, as well as his highly anticipated fourth novel, The Thorn of Emberlain. "It is something that I am absolutely working on and trying to be as open and honest about as possible," he says. But he took a quick break from writing elaborate fantasy heists to show me around the treasure-filled vault of his Steam library.
What game are you currently playing? I have reopened Morrowind for the first time in a number of years. Right around the time I was working on my first novel and had not finished it yet, I was playing it on the original Xbox. Other than the fact I was like 23, 24, I can't fathom how I did that.
I've been meaning to go back to Morrowind for ages, but I was put off by the jankiness of the UI, the quality-of-life experience, or the thought that there were just enough rough edges of this game that's now nearly a quarter of a century old, that I wouldn't enjoy it.
I was talking to another author who maybe has a bad computer game habit, and he turned me on to OpenMW. He posted some screenshots on Bluesky of some beautiful-looking Morrowind vistas and some nice skies and vegetation. And I thought "A-ha! Here's a man that uses mods." So even though I own a copy of Morrowind, like the fourth copy I've bought in my life, I'm now using OpenMW, and I'm loving it.
The thing that I enjoy about Morrowind is the incredible granularity of its various subsystems and the game-breaking things that you can do with processes like alchemy and enchantment. And the fact you can enchant layers of clothing and be wearing enchanted underwear underneath your enchanted armour. [But] I set a bunch of rules for my character, because usually I play something along the lines of a wizard who can go anywhere, do anything, build high-powered potions to fly all over the landscape at high speed.
I decided that I would play something along the template of a Paladin, and I gave myself a very limited powerset that I could create utilising the custom spell-builders … so I have a very limited toolset, and I opted to spend more time actually wandering around the world doing quests, and less time sitting in one place making 10,000 potions.
I played Skyrim to death [with] many character concepts, and one of my favourites was a little ruleset that I called the Conan playthrough, where you play as melee-type character who cannot use magic at all … you place all these rules and limitations upon yourself. What I found is that narrowing the focus of the game experience can be as liberating as having a completely open world before you, and I've rediscovered that with this particular Morrowind playthrough.
What was the previous game you played, and is it still installed? It's a game from the late '90s called Star Wars: Rebellion, which over in the UK would have been known as Star Wars: Supremacy. It's elderly, it's janky, its UI and its quality of life are from a previous era of human development. It's absolutely full of problems. But it's also got kernels of brilliance, and there's never been anything like it ever since. As a Star Wars fan, I find myself returning to it over and over, as a dog to his vomit.
What is the oldest game (by release date) currently installed on your PC? I've still got Master of Orion 2 , and it's still playable, which is from '90s. I love MOO2. I've played it to death in every possible permutation. I last played Master of Orion about five years ago. That would have also been in the pandemic.
You can see how nearly every game in the 4X space has been trying for the last three decades to, in some fashion, be that game and recreate its experience, and that's a very difficult thing to do … MOO2 just has a certain smoothness to it.
I've tried to get into other 4X games … but I just don't think that any 4X space game since MOO2 has successfully emulated that smoothness of pickup and that open sense of play, as in "Where's my civilization going to go?"
To a certain extent when you play a game like MOO2, outside the bounds of creating a custom species and a custom culture, you're playing with somebody else's IP, and when I play a game like that, I look for a certain degree of possessiveness, a certain degree of personalisation. I want to play my species' story and I don't necessarily want to play with somebody else's narrative IP.
What is the highest number of hours you have in any given game, according to Steam? All right, let's look at the embarrassing total. All I'm going to say about this is that if J.R.R Tolkien had had a Steam account, his numbers would be pretty embarrassing too.

pool.titulo: ¿Por qué Jason es tan callado y reservado en GTA 6? Rockstar ha explicado que una película de 1972 inspiró su personalidad
pool.resumen:
Millones de personas están disfrutando Grand Theft Auto 6 , y todavía hay muchos que siguen en la isla de Key Lento con Jason Duval , uno de los protagonistas del juego. Lo que más ha llamado la atención de los jugadores ha sido su personalidad tan tímida y reservada , lo que contrasta con la actitud más impulsiva y expresiva de Lucía Caminos. Rockstar ha diseñado a los dos personajes para que se complementen y aporten más profundidad a la relación que mantienen a lo largo de la historia.
La película de 1972 que inspiró la personalidad de Jason en GTA 6
Sin embargo, lo que desconocíamos hasta ahora es que Rockstar se inspiró en una película de hace más de 50 años para construir la personalidad de Jason, tomando como referencia a un actor que decía más con sus silencios que por lo que salía de su boca. Nos referimos a Steve McQueen . Rupert Humphries, vicepresidente sénior de narrativa de Rockstar, le ha explicado al medio Destructoid cómo se inspiraron para dar forma al reservado carácter de Jason. El equipo se puso a buscar películas de parejas a la fuga y la que más destacó fue La Huida, estrenada en 1972 .

pool.resumen: What good is a powerful gaming PC without a monitor capable of showcasing its glory?
pool.contenido:
Dell makes some of the best gaming monitors around under the Alienware brand. Its OLED monitors are no different. They source the same panels used in the highest end LG and Samsung OLED monitors and add on a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in. For Black Friday, most of Dell's newest 2026 and 2025 monitors have dropped to new price lows . These include smaller sizes like the 27" Alienware AWAW2726DM to bigger sizes like the recently released 39" Alienware AW3926QW. Check out all the Black Friday deals below.
During this Black Friday season, get an additional 3X back in Dell rewards with every monitor purchase. You will need to sign up for a Dell Rewards membership, which is free to join.
27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD QD-OLED Gaming Monitor Most people would agree that OLED monitors are as good as it gets for gaming. They're also really expensive. Well, Alienware is bucking the trend with one of its latest 2026 OLED releases. The 27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED gaming monitor is listed at an already reasonable retail price of $349.99, but for Black Friday it's down to just $279.99 with free shipping. This is a 27" 2560x1440 (QHD) monitor that incorporates a Samsung quantum dot OLED ( QD OLED ) panel, which is brighter and has a wider color gamut than the more commonly found W-OLED panel.
39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology."It launched with a retail price of $1,099.99 but for Black Friday you can get it for $100 less . The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive inclusion is the LG RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.
The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.
32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K 240Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor Alienware's most popular 4K OLED gaming monitor is also down to its lowest price ever. For Black Friday, you can pick up a 32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K QD OLED gaming monitor for just $699.99 with free shipping. The AW3225QF is a rare gaming monitor that combines a native 4K resolution, 240Hz refresh rate , and a gorgeous Samsung-sourced quantum dot OLED panel. If you're looking for the best 4K gaming monitor , this should definitely be on your short list. The Alienware AW3225QF is HDR True Black 400 certified with up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness. It also boasts a factory calibrated 99.3% DCI-P3 color range, 1700R curve, and G-Sync certification .
32" Alienware AW3226Q 4K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor The 32" Alienware AW3226Q gaming monitor is another recent release that's aimed toward the more budget-conscious crowd. The monitor launched about a month ago at a very reasonable $699.99 price tag, but it's already $50 off ahead of Black Friday. Unlike the slighty more expensive AW3225QF which uses a curved 240Hz QD-OLED panel from Samsung, the Alienware AW3226Q is equipped with a flat panel 165Hz RGB stripe tandem OLED panel from LG. In exchange for a lower refresh rate and no official G-Sync certification (it's still G-Sync compatible), you get better text clarity and arguably a better monitor for non-gaming use.

New for 2026: Sonos Beam Ultra Soundbar The Sonos Beam Ultra is more than just an incremental upgrade over its Gen 2 predecessor. Like the Arc Ultra compared to the Arc , this is practically an entirely different soundbar. Although the size profile isn't much different (29 inches long vs 25 inches), the Beam Ultra now houses a total of nine total speakers instead of five. This improves the Beam's surround sound capabilities two-fold: (1) it is now technically a 7.1.2ch system instead of 5.1.2ch and (2) it has two physical upfiring speakers for true Dolby Atmos support whereas the previous Beam Gen 2 used virtual height channels for a simulated Atmos experience. Other upgrades include AI speech enhanced to isolate and amplify dialogue, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, and USB-C line-in. It also has a microphone for voice control.
New for 2026: Sonos Ace Ultra Headphones The Sonos Ace Ultra has also undergone major renovation, which isn't as surprising since the original Ace was Sonos' first foray into the world of over-ear headphones. pool.titulo: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Plows Through GTA 6 Hype With $225 Million Opening Weekend
pool.resumen: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took GTA 6 players off of their couches and into movie theaters with a staggering estimated box office total of $225 million in its opening weekend.
pool.contenido:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took GTA 6 players off of their couches and into movie theaters with a staggering estimated box office total of $225 million in its opening weekend.
The latest prequel in Suzanne Collins' run of Hunger Games adaptations attracted more than just fans, pulling in a whopping $125 million domestically and $105 million internationally following its November 20 release date. It's an impressive debut that proved the dystopia franchise has more than enough staying power, even in the face of the biggest entertainment launch of all time .
Attracting moviegoers to take a break from Vice City this weekend was star Joseph Zada (We Were Liars), who stars as a young Haymitch Abernathy to tell the story of the Second Quarter Quell and the impact it had on the Hunger Games for all time. A brutal flick that IGN gave an 8/10 review , Sunrise on the Reaping is an adaptation of Collins' book of the same name, which originally released in March 2025. Its star-studded cast also includes Jesse Plemons (Game Night) as Plutarch Heavensbee, Ralph Fiennes (28 Years Later) as President Snow, Glenn Close (Fatal Attraction) as Drusilla Sickle, Mckenna Grace (Five Nights at Freddy's 2) as Maysilee Donner, and more.
"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is one of the strongest entries of the franchise because of its excellent performances," we said in our review, "especially Joseph Zada’s compassionate turn as young Haymitch. It also closes the story of Panem on a high note."
The mainline Hunger Games movies took a break after catching up with the Katniss Everdeen saga that began with Collins' books. The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, a novel focused on a teenage Coriolanus Snow, launched in 2020 and was adapted into a film of the same name in 2023. That project, which starred Billy the Kid's Tom Blyth, landed atop the box office upon its debut, though with decidedly softer results that saw its global opening weekend reach $98.5 million .
Sunrise on the Reaping has now brought the focus back to the good guys, and to much success. The new Hunger Games movie had a hefty production budget of $150 million, according to Variety . With plenty of time left in theaters before heavy hitters like Dune: Part 3 and Avengers: Doomsday sweep theaters mid-December, Lionsgate is almost certainly happy with its first few days.
Despite appealing enough to moviegoers to sneak in an explosive theatrical debut right under GTA's nose, there's actually no word on whether audiences will see a new story set in Panem anytime soon. Collins has not announced any additional books set in that universe as of right now, but with so many characters and stories ripe for exploration, it probably wouldn't be too much of a surprise to see The Hunger Games back in theaters at some point.
Elsewhere at the box office for the late November weekend was Johnny Depp's Ebenezer , which racked up another $22 million. The grim Christmas Carol reimagining earned $42 million worldwide when it premiered last weekend. IGN gave it a 6/10 review . The top five box office earners and their global totals for the weekend are as follows:
1. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ($225 million)
2. Ebenezer ($22 million)
3. Ramayana ($13.765 million)
4. I Play Rocky ($13.111 million)
5. The Cat in the Hat (10.55 million)
While we wait to see if Collins returns with another book, you can check out everything you need to know before seeing Sunrise on the Reaping . You can also read one IGN writer's explanation for why the movie commits the cardinal sin of prequels .
