pool.titulo: GTA 6 Dev Honors Late Mother With In-Game Memorial That Players Can Visit
pool.resumen: A GTA 6 developer has paid tribute to his late mother with an in-game memorial in Leonida that players can find and visit for themselves.
pool.contenido:
A GTA 6 developer has paid tribute to his late mother with an in-game memorial in Leonida that players can find and visit themselves.
Rockstar Games QA developer Matt Green shared the touching story of how his mother helped launch his career in game development and the way she was honored in the Grand Theft Auto universe with a post on Instagram. Although she passed eight months before GTA 6's launch last week, Rockstar still managed to include her in a wall of other names in a memorial located in Leonida.
"As a kid, I remember practically begging my Mum to let me get GTA: Vice City and even though she was understandably reluctant, she caved," Green said. "I think that decision is likely what set me on the path to eventually working at Rockstar Games and on GTA VI.
"She was super proud and excited to see what I'd been working on but unfortunately I never got to show her. She's been gone almost 8 months now and sometimes it still doesn't feel real."
The memorial, which Green said can be found "just north of Hamlet, shows that Bev Green passed in March 2026, and she's joined by a collection of other names, too. It's unclear if every name on the memorial is tied to another Rockstar developer's lost loved one or who the names may be referencing, but we know at least two other names are.
Production designer Terrance Radcliff took to X/Twitter to share how the team had immortalized his father and daughter, who both passed during GTA 6's development. Elhuntry Radcliff and Jade Radcliff can be seen next to each other in-game.
"To wrap up launch week, what an honor to see my Father and my first Daughter, Jade, both of who I lost during development, forever immortalized in GTA VI," Radcliff said. "To have them be a part of such a huge moment in gaming history means everything to me. Peace & blessings."
To wrap up launch week, what an honor to see my Father and my first Daughter, Jade, both of who I lost during development, forever immortalized in GTA VI. To have them be a part of such a huge moment in gaming history means everything to me. Peace & blessings. 🙏🏽 #GTAVI https://t.co/HKOFYBiIR9
— Terrance (@SincereSounds) November 22, 2026
"I'm incredibly grateful that she's able to be honoured inside the world of VI," Green's post added. "Miss you Mum."
With Green's guidance, we tracked down the memorial for those who would like to visit it and pay their respects. If you're looking to make a visit to pay your respects, look no further than the images below.

pool.titulo: Rockstar Says Darts Were Cut From GTA 6 Because It Didn't Have 'Unlimited Money or Time' to Make It 'Feel Proper'
pool.resumen: Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6, but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.
pool.contenido:
Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6 , but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.
Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained why the studio chose to focus on some aspects of development and not others during an interview with VGC . As noted by the site, picking up a game of darts has proven to be a good pastime in games like GTA 5 and GTA Online, but in GTA 6, the standards were a bit higher.
From NPCs to the feel of motorized scooters, Leonida is Rockstar's most realistic playground yet. Every blade of grass was given special attention, and while pool was one game the team was able to fully realize, not everything panned out like they had hoped. Nelson said "darts was a contentious one" when talking about the decision to cut it from the game, explaining that it was left behind because the team didn't have the resources to do it right.
"Even we… you hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to," he said.
Nelson elaborated, saying that, starting with Red Dead Redemption 2, the team started to treat mini-games more like activities. In other words, bonuses like darts became less about being a diversion of Rockstar's open worlds and more of an extension of them. The goal is to make pool, darts, or any other activity feel like it's just as punchy and weighty for Jason and Lucia as it is in the real world.
Using GTA 6's in-game workouts as an example, he added, "You’re not just pushing a button; it mimics what weightlifting is."
"A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right," Nelson continued. "Darts is one we just didn’t get to."
Long story short, Rockstar just "didn't have the resources" to make it "feel proper." His thoughts on the matter – or any scenario where a mechanic or activity is cut – were summed up in one line: "It’s better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough."
GTA 6 is now the highest-rated game of all time . IGN gave it a 10/10 review .
For one of the better examples of the care the developers put into side activities, look no further than some of the games Jason has on his JoySystem . You can see how Rockstar pulled from real-world inspirations to create his character here .

pool.titulo: Amazon and Target Launch '3 for 2' Sales on Books, Box Sets, and Vinyl for Black Friday

Target has officially launched its main Black Friday sale, which means Amazon is now matching all of the best deals in its own sale . This is especially good news for anyone looking to pad their book or vinyl collections this year thanks to the popular '3 for 2' sale returning at both major retailers ahead of Thanksgiving.
This is actually the second time the two retailers have had this type of sale in November, but this time around there seems to be a lot more included here. That's especially true if you're looking to grab multiple box sets at a discount. This sale is arguably the best time to buy books at a discount if you're willing to spend a bit more to get the extra savings.
Buy 2, Get 1 Free Sale on Books and Music For those who aren't already familiar with this sale, the way it works is pretty easy to understand. All you need to do is add three eligible items to your cart and the least expensive one will get discounted from the price at check out. Because of this, you'll want to buy three similarly priced items to maximize the discount you're getting. You can also mix and match anything in the sale, so you don't need to just buy three books or three vinyl records.
Our Book Recommendations The book portion of this sale is quite massive, so it's definitely worth diving into all of the book inclusions to see what's there. If you're looking for some recommendations on where to get started, however, I've picked out some of the most interesting titles I could find.
The Dungeon Crawler Carl books on sale here are always incredibly popular during these sales. Matt Dinniman's LitRPG series has really blown up this year and it's a great opportunity to pick up the full collection for pretty cheap. It's also worth checking out Pierce Brown's Red Rising series , which has been hitting the zeitgeist again after the movie adaptation news earlier this year . And if you're into romantasy, Sarah J. Maas' latest ACOTAR book is even included here.
If you're just looking for some cool stuff to add to your shelf, I'd recommend checking out Hyrule Historia first. This is an art book that details the long and interesting Legend of Zelda history. There are also illustrated versions of Lord of the Rings and Harry Potter included here this year.
Our Box Set Recommendations The box sets included in the sale are the best overall deal for anyone looking to start their book collection. These are higher-priced items that include either all of the books in a series or a good chunk of them at once. They will often also feature some sort of cool artwork on the spines that look wonderful together on your shelf.
As for what you should check out first, I recommend grabbing The Witcher books on sale here. These books spawned one of the most successful video game franchises of all time and, according to the author , will still be getting new stories. I'd recommend the Game of Thrones box set for similar reasons, but George R.R. Martin may never finish that series so dive into those books at your own risk.
There are also some great fantasy box sets that have since been turned into movies or TV shows. The Hunger Games box set includes the latest prequel, Sunrise on the Reaping, which is now in theaters. There's also the Percy Jackson books , which is worth reading alongside season 3 of the Disney+ adaptation . And if you don't already own all of the Harry Potter books , the paperback set is definitely worth grabbing ahead of HBO's TV show next month.
Our Vinyl recommendations
The sale on music is just as robust as the book selection. So although I've picked out some of the things I personally think are cool, I encourage you to check out the full inclusion list for yourself and search for albums you know you like.
That being said, my overall top pick in the sale is the Lord of the Rings trilogy. Howard Shore's music helped turn Peter Jackson's movies into something truly epic. This is an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a good LOTR gift to buy someone this year.
A few of my other top picks include classics like Michael Jackson's Thriller, Metallica's Master of Puppets, and the Beatle's Abby Road. Noah Khan's Stick Season is also included here as it's been one of the most popular albums of the last few years.

pool.titulo: Binding of Isaac DLC adds AI music in GTA 6-parodying update despite not having an AI disclosure, Steam reviews drop to Overwhelmingly Negative, music gets pulled
pool.resumen: "Woke up to a shit show," Edmund McMillen wrote.
pool.contenido:
While most videogames got out of the way of Grand Theft Auto 6, on the day of its release The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth's free online DLC Repentance+ released an update. It included an easter egg daily challenge called Crime Mode (the seed is V1CE BSMT) with references to GTA like a wanted rating, guns, cops, and cars. Well, driveable minecarts.
What should have been an easy PR win for publisher Nicalis quickly turned sour as players pointed out that the music in Crime Mode sure sounds AI-generated . "It has that 'tinniness' that something like Suno generated music has", user ShweetStuff noted before looking at the music files and finding that, yep, there was Suno metadata in the file comments . Yet there was no AI disclosure on the DLC's Steam page.
Players were not thrilled by this development. Steam user reviews on The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ dropped to Overwhelmingly Negative, with only 8% positive recent reviews. Players put the blame on Nicalis, who licence Binding of Isaac from its original creator Edmund McMillen. "Edmund please take back control of the game", one said.
"Woke up to a shit show," McMillen wrote on the hatesite formerly known as Twitter when he found out what had happened, "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."
As of the latest update, the AI-generated music is gone. "It's a little sad given Joey Kuras (game's sound designer) did some excellent sounds for Mewgenics", ShweetStuff wrote, "but I suppose this is the industry nowadays!"

pool.titulo: SNEG has re-released three more venerable PC strategy games including Warlords 4: Heroes of Etheria
pool.resumen: Let the war begin.
pool.contenido:
As well as giving a spit-and-polish digital release to various Warhammer classics , antique D&D games , and the cult ellipsoid horror games in the Ecstatica series , SNEG has been bug-fixing a bunch of strategy games from years gone by and getting them up on Steam and GOG. The latest trio to appear on digital platforms are Theocracy, Soldiers at War, and Warlords 4: Heroes of Etheria.
Warlords 4 was the final turn-based game in the beloved series, with the RTS spin-off series Warlords Battlecry already two games deep by the time of its release in 2003. This updated version supports resolutions up to 4K, and incorporates community fixes and a community-made campaign. It's available on Steam and GOG .
Soldiers at War took the X-COM/UFO turn-based tactics formula—this was 1998, X-COM still had a hyphen—and applied it to World War II. You'd choose a squad of eight from your platoon of 32 each mission, fighting through a campaign that started in North Africa and ended in Germany, gaining experience along the way. SNEG's version supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution. It's available on Steam and GOG .
Theocracy narrowly beat Total War to the punch in March of 2000 with its mix of turn-based civilization management and real-time battles, tasking you with uniting Aztec tribes before the prophesied Spanish invasion. You're on the clock with 100 years to use diplomacy, trade, and warfare to bring together an empire that can stand the test of time. The updated version still has a resolution of 800x600, but uses FSR 1 to scale up for modern displays. You'll be shocked to learn, it's also available on Steam and GOG .
All three games are designed to be easy to run on modern Windows systems, and have cloud saves and achievements. I'm tempted by Warlords 4, which I didn't play at the time because I'd moved over to the real-time Battlecry games by then. But I've still got fond memories of Warlords 2 Deluxe, which had 60 different worlds so if you were tired of raising griffon armies in its generic fantasy land you could conquer something oddball like Dante's Inferno instead. Or even make your own, right down to pixel-crafting the unit art. Good times.

pool.titulo: Nvidia released a hotfix for its driver hammering your SSD, but it doesn't actually work
pool.resumen: AI isn't great at fixing problems AI created.
pool.contenido:
Over the last couple of weeks, some Nvidia users noticed their SSDs were taking a hammering , reporting their driver's log file was being overwritten constantly, sometimes to the tune of 30 GB every hour. Which obviously isn't great for the lifespan of the valuable SSD you've got it installed on.
Given the problem was caused by recent driver updates, rolling back to version 621.01 was the best solution until Nvidia could do something about it. Which they did, releasing a hotfix as version 621.35 . It's not available in the GeForce app yet, but you can download it directly from Nvidia's site. Not that you should.
As users on the Nvidia subreddit are reporting, the problem persists. While the hotfix reduces the peak write rate and prevents it for a short while after reboot, it eventually creeps back in. One user reported that overnight the log file was still being rewritten by approximately 4.5 GB every hour.
So yeah, the best solution remains to roll back to version 621.01 and, as always with Nvidia drivers, to hold off on updating to the latest driver until it's been confirmed safe. If this ongoing saga sounds familiar, it's because the same thing happened to AMD's GPU drivers earlier this month. Maybe vibecoding driver updates and then vibecoding fixes for their inevitable bugs isn't the best way of doing things.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 The End of the Road: Should you swim for it, or choose no surrender?
pool.resumen: A choice (or two!) can lead to drastically different endings.
pool.contenido:
Please note, this guide contains massive spoilers for some of the endings of Grand Theft Auto 6 . If you don't want to know what happens, please stop reading!
There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and not all the endings take place in the same location. One of the potential final scenes during the GTA 6 story mission , The End of the Road, takes place on a bridge in the Leonida Keys.
After discovering the cops are onto them, Jason and Lucia drive away from Cal's house and head to Brian's marina to find an airplane. The police quickly trap them on a bridge with a roadblock ahead and multiple cars behind them. Lucia wants to keep going but Jason thinks it's all over for them. The player is then given a choice, "Swim for it" or "No Surrender."
AGAIN, MASSIVE SPOILERS BELOW! STOP NOW IF YOU DON'T WANT TO KNOW THE ENDINGS !
No Surrender Jason and Lucia decide Tomas is better off without them in his life. They drive through the roadblock, shooting at the cops. They're both shot to death and we see them dead in the front seat of the car, still holding hands. During the end credits, we see Tomas living happily with Lucia's sister and her husband and children.
Swim for it (A, B, and C) Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim to freedom.
However, a second choice appears once you've chosen 'Swim for it.' As Jason gets out of the car, a prompt for Lucia to 'Exit' the car appears. You can choose for Lucia to follow through with the plan by pressing the button, or change your mind and let the prompt expire.
A: 'Swim for it' and 'Exit' : The couple will get out of the car together and walk to the edge of the bridge. Lucia jumps but Jason does not, letting himself get arrested by the cops. During the credits, Lucia signs the deal which keeps her free and sends Jason to prison. We see her bring Tomas to visit him, so Jason finally meets his son, though it's through glass.
B: 'Swim for it' and don't 'Exit' : If you choose to swim for it but don't choose the 'Exit' prompt, Jason will get out of the car but Lucia will remain in the car. The police will open fire and kill them both. As with the No Surrender option, we see Tomas living with Lucia's sister's family.
C: 'Swim for it' and 'Exit' (with $2 million in Buck Me savings) : If you delayed the Protective Custody mission of GTA 6 until you had deposited $2 million in savings, the Swim for it and Exit choices will show the same results, but during the credits, Lucia uses the money to get Jason released from prison. Lucia picks him up at prison, and Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.
Note: These are not the only endings to GTA 6. I've seen several more endings that do not take place on the bridge at all and don't involve these particular choices.

pool.titulo: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
pool.resumen: Bye-bye, Blueprints.
pool.contenido:
Unreal Engine 6 will not launch with the engine's long-standard Blueprints scripting system. The news came in a Friday, November 19 post on the Unreal Engine website , written by Epic Games executive vice president of development, Marcus Wassmer. Here's Wassmer's top-level summary from the post:
Blueprints have not (and it appears, will not) be deprecated in Unreal Engine 5, and the company maintains that projects will still be easy to convert from UE5 to UE6. Wassmer cited a declining cost in AI task completion as one reason for this belief, as well as the team's ongoing, but apparently successful conversion of Fortnite's Blueprint library to UE6's Verse programming language through an AI-assisted process.
Blueprints are a widely-used feature of Unreal. Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek, an AI skeptic, has put out a vlog on the subject . Essentially, Faliszek argues that Blueprints (and features like them in other game engines) represent a middle ground between artistic and technical work, an introduction and skill builder for less technically-minded developers. Without them, such developers seemingly have to either learn Verse code, or integrate LLM prompting into their workflows.
"We made a new skill in the middle there, between normal and expert," Faliszek said of intermediate tools like Blueprints. "To lose that determinism from game design, and instead have to prompt AI⁠—or write your own Verse … It's losing those tools that made all those designers and all those artists so powerful, to be able to do really powerful things and have access to really deep-down things, but in a safe way that the engineers can decide what that meant to them."
A dark horse game of the year candidate, the first-person RPG Queen's Domain , was made with Unreal Engine. I recently spoke to co-developer Eric Berger, who specialized in art and design alongside the more technically-focused Bradley Boothe, a relationship that rhymes with the ones Faliszek outlined in his video.
I spoke to Berger before seeing Epic's latest press release, but Berger already indicated that Unreal's AI pivot is prompting Freshly Baked Games to switch engines for its next project. I followed up with Berger about this Blueprint news, and the developer said that Blueprints were a major part of the workflow on Queen's Domain.
I'm a layman in game development, but I think Wassmer's post elides that there is a large qualitative difference between doing any work via LLM prompt versus the old-fashioned way⁠—I don't like or want to use these tools, myself, and I don't think that's an unpopular stance. Commenter ZILtoid1991 on Faliszek's video compared the move to Apple removing headphone jacks on the iPhone, a comparison I find fruitful.
It was hugely unpopular at the time, and is still derided by enthusiasts, but it also worked . Other manufacturers copied Apple, and everybody has bluetooth headphones now⁠—or Apple's own, proprietary Air Pods. But Apple had far less success trying something similar with its laptops: The lack of ports on late 2010s Macbooks proved disastrous, and Apple has since reintroduced more (and a wider variety of) ports on newer models of the popular line. I certainly have my own anti-AI, pro-headphone jack preferences, but we'll have to see how this plays out with the Unreal Engine.

Un congresista de Estados Unidos quiere proteger los videojuegos que ya hemos comprado En Estados Unidos están intentando hacer lo mismo , concretamente Alejandro Frost, representante demócrata por Florida, que anunció el 18 de noviembre la iniciativa Protect Our Games Act en un evento virtual sobre la propiedad de los videojuegos . "Cuando alguien te dice que vas a comprar algo, lo estás comprando. Y deberías poder tenerlo para siempre , se apaguen o no los servidores". Una de las medidas que plantea es que los jugadores puedan crear y gestionar sus propios servidores si cierran los oficiales.

pool.titulo: Kate Bishop Actress Hailee Steinfeld Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday
pool.resumen: Marvel Studios has confirmed Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld as a last-minute addition to the cast of Avengers: Doomsday.
pool.contenido:
Marvel Studios has confirmed Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld as a last-minute addition to the cast of Avengers: Doomsday .
Marvel Studios announced the surprise return of Hawkeye's Disney+ partner in a nonchalant Instagram reel tonight. Serving as promotion for Steinfeld's other new Disney movie, Hexed, the video sees her jokingly say someone delivered a chair "from a different movie," but the post's caption makes things pretty clear.
"Catch Hailee Steinfeld in Disney's Hexed before she returns in Avengers: Doomsday," the post said.
You'd be forgiven for thinking Steinfeld was already included in Doomsday's already enormous lineup of superheroes and A-listers. Everyone from Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal to Tom Hiddleston has previously been confirmed to make an appearance of some kind, but Steinfeld was one of a few names to have been curiously benched up until this point.
She first appeared as the bow-wielding Kate Bishop in the Jeremy Renner-led 2021 show, Hawkeye . Aside from a The Marvels cameo and some animated voice work, Steinfeld hasn't spent too much time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as the multiverse saga has rolled on. That won't stop her from helping out in the first chapter of its finale, though.
With the cast already stacked, it's hard to know just how prominently her character will be featured amongst the chaos. Between the Avengers, the New Avengers, Fantastic Four, and X-Men, there will likely be little room to explore how she gets along with the rest of the crew. For many, just the fact that she'll help in the fight against Doctor Doom is probably enough.
Avengers: Doomsday premieres December 18, 2026. That's a little less than one month away, but Marvel's made it clear that it's saved plenty of surprises .
Another major MCU name was teased for the movie when VisionQuest wrapped up earlier this month. Fans are expecting at least one more trailer to drop between now and the film's premiere, and if Captain Carter actress Hayley Atwell is to be believed , we won't have to wait much longer to see it.

pool.titulo: En 1976 los arqueólogos dejaron sin excavar parte de una casa romana en Mérida. 50 años después, unos estudiantes encuentran allí pinturas murales con aves y escenas mitológicas
pool.resumen:
En la Huerta de Otero, en Mérida , se encuentra una estructura del Imperio Romano que, según los expertos, superaría los 5.000 metros cuadrados. Tras descubrirse en 1976 por un equipo de arqueólogos, lo más impresionante no es que aún a día de hoy se sigan encontrando restos fantásticamente conservados. Lo realmente increíble es que apenas hemos visto el 15% de todo el edificio.
La culpa la tiene haber parado la investigación del yacimiento, que quedó prácticamente abandonado poco después de ese descubrimiento y que, gracias a un grupo de estudiantes de arqueología , en 2019 volvió a ponerse manos a la obra. El espectacular mosaico descubierto en 2023 les empujó a seguir trabajando y, mientras siguen retirando la tierra que protege la estructura, han aparecido nuevas pinturas.
Las pinturas que escondía la casa de Medusa
Por los frescos encontrados se cree que aquel rincón era una casa señorial en la que los pavos reales, estrechamente ligados a las clases más altas de la estructura social romana, cobran una vital importancia. El mosaico, que ya va por los 30 metros cuadrados , contiene también la cabeza de una Medusa .

La clave está en cómo esas instalaciones adicionales utilizan la energía solar térmica para seguir produciendo energía cuando no hay sol directo. Estamos acostumbrados a que las ciudades crezcan con formas estructuralmente caóticas, expandiéndose alrededor de plazas, alargándose de forma perpendicular entre cruces de caminos, o ampliándose sin ton ni son alrededor de barrios que terminan chocando con la expansión de otros. A pocos kilómetros de Cracovia, al sur de Polonia , el pueblo de En Sułoszowa encontró otro camino. Uno, para ser más concretos.
Sus viviendas y edificios se amontonan a lo largo de nueve kilómetros de carretera haciendo de esa calle la única vía principal. Con terrenos justo detrás de las casas, dando así lugar a pintorescas y coloridas parcelas que hacen que ver la ciudad desde arriba sea como ver un pueblo de videojuego, en realidad esa forma de construir lleva muchos años entre nosotros y hasta tiene nombre propio: ulicówki.
La genialidad de construir un pueblo en una sola calle

pool.titulo: Naughty Dog Dev: GTA 6 Appears to Him as ‘as a Bugatti Veyron Would to a Nervous Victorian Child’
pool.resumen: Developers are stunned at how dramatically advanced GTA 6 is.
pool.contenido:
Just like the rest of us, developers the world over are playing GTA 6. Just like the rest of us, they’re also finding themselves blown away by just how dramatically advanced and impressive GTA 6 is proving to be. However, as professionals with a far, far firmer idea of how the sausage gets made than regular punters, precisely how impressed some developers are is speaking volumes about just what a technical achievement GTA 6 really does represent.
Naughty Dog world design director Michael Barclay, presently working on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, minces no words.
“I’ve made video games for 19 years and GTA VI appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child,” writes Barclay via social media.
Barclay is far from alone, with a host of developers in the replies to Barclay’s comment expressing like sentiments in the days following GTA 6’s release.
Payday 2 game director David Goldfarb, who previously worked on Mirror’s Edge and a variety of Battlefield games, is similarly stunned.
“Been making games over 30 years… Can’t even find words for what I’m playing now,” he writes , later noting he’s “never been this floored by anything ever.”
Character artist Del Walker (Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League, The Last of Us: Part II, Star Wars: Jedi - Survivor) quips he simply can’t explain what he’s seeing despite his background in the business.
“Every GTA clip gets sent to me in the group chat with. ‘You’re a game dev. How did they do this?” he writes. “Brother, I wasn’t there when they opened the portal? This is not magic I recognize.”
GTA 6 arrived late last week, smashing records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with retail sales reaching $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours. In my review for IGN I called it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” something that is making increasingly more sense to me the more other developers I note making comments like the above.
Just getting started in GTA 6, or wondering what to do next? You can get stuck into the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN, consult our Beginner's Guide or Leonida interactive map , or get an idea of all the incredible flourishes to keep an eye out for by checking out our look at 99 incredible details you can find in GTA 6.

pool.titulo: Robbing Banks is a Blast, But I Wish There Were More Houses to Repair in GTA 6
pool.resumen: Forget sticking things up with a shotgun, I want to fix things up with a nailgun.
pool.contenido:
My first weekend with Grand Theft Auto 6 was truly mindblowing. The first 20 or so hours I’ve spent with Rockstar’s triumphant return to Vice City have transported me to an impossibly high fidelity game world and treated me to criminal capers so immaculately crafted they make Michael Mann seem more like a Michael mouse. As I’ve made my way across the sprawling Leonida map I’ve relished each and every unethical exploit of lawbreaking lovebirds, Jason and Lucia. So far I’ve been Jason the wheelman, Jason the bagman, and Jason the hitman, but to my surprise, what I really want to be is… Tim the Toolman?
Before you hit me with one of Tim Allen’s trademark quizzical caveman grunts, let me back up for a moment. In case you’re not one of the more than 20 million players who gleefully jumped into Rockstar’s latest crime epic on day one, GTA 6’s opening hours present a number of optional tasks that you can undertake as Jason in an effort to make his girlfriend Lucia’s arrival at your love nest a little more loved-up. You can visit the grocery store to line the kitchen pantry with protein bars and packets of chips, pick up a bouquet of flowers, and even splash out on a customised necklace from a local jeweler if you really want to boost your relationship status to Boyfriend of the Year levels.
I ticked off these tasks more out of open-world obligation than any particularly earnest desire to impress my virtual girlfriend; they were pink dots on my minimap, so my well-trained gamer instincts compelled me to clear them. But what I did derive a surprising amount of satisfaction from, was running down the shortlist of repairs to Jason’s dilapidated waterfront home. Drilling in drywall panels in the bedroom and applying a warm shade of peach-coloured paint to them with a roller. Climbing a ladder onto the roof and fastening fresh shingles to it with a nailgun to stop the ceiling leaks. Replacing the rotten steps leading to the front door with some fresh planks of wood. Each of these tasks provided me with moments of zen far more relaxing than the game's own dedicated meditation minigame. I even took a moment to stop and marvel at the impeccably well-rendered tools in Jason’s shed.
I enjoyed fussing around on Jason’s fixer-upper so much that I must admit I was a little deflated to discover that once this brief burst of renovations are complete, that seems to be it as far as the cosy home makeover minigames are concerned. A lot of the other features of GTA 6 are presented as an appetite-whetting taster before they become ongoing activities to pursue at your leisure for the rest of the story; you go on a short hunting trip with one of Jason’s old army buddies, and from then on you’re free to stalk deer and bears in the Leonida wilderness. You complete a dirt-encrusted drive in an opening event at the Thrillbilly Mud Club, and afterwards you’re free to indulge in spectacular stunt jumps, hill climbs, and a variety of races on the MotorStorm-style circuits.
Completing Jason’s home repairs, however, doesn’t seem to unlock any form of handyman activities to pursue around the map. I envisaged clearing out the longarms and bulletproof vests stashed in the bed of Jason’s truck and loading it up with power tools and paint cans to go do some odd jobs around the neighbourhood – or perhaps even buying run-down properties, fixing them up, and then flipping them to quickly boost Jason and Lucia’s shared bank account. But after speaking with other members of IGN who’ve rolled credits in GTA 6, it doesn’t sound like Jason ever gets another opportunity to pick up his tools again, other than to grab a hammer or shovel to smack hillbillies around with when he’s in the process of stealing the profits from their meth lab.
Now, I know what you’re thinking reading this; if he wanted to do home restorations in a video game, there’s no shortage of quality options out there that could scratch that itch, from The Sims 4 to House Flipper to Powerwash Simulator. I also know what you’re thinking if you happen to be my wife reading this; there’s no shortage of DIY projects I could be spending my Saturday doing around my actual house instead of sitting on the couch complaining of the lack of virtual repair jobs to complete in a video game. (I’ll get to them next weekend, I promise.)
However, I think a big part of the reason that I’d like to do more repairwork in GTA 6 is because this is undoubtedly the most beautiful and believable game world I’ve ever inhabited, and thus I feel an innate urge to preserve it. In fact, unlike any GTA game before it, I’ve found myself really focussing on how much life there is in the environment as opposed to creating my typical trails of death, strapping on a scuba tank and playing with porpoises in the depths of the Atlantic Ocean, or peering at pelicans through the in-game binoculars. I’m only a couple of chapters into the story, but so far I wholeheartedly agree with Luke Reilly’s 10 out of 10 review . GTA 6 is clearly a masterpiece, and one that doesn’t really leave much room for improvement. But, even so, I can’t help but wish it had a few more rooms for improvement.
GTA 6 doesn't leave much room for improvement, but I wish it had a few more rooms for improvement. These are the things I’m thinking about as I drive around Vice City and its surroundings. While most players are probably scanning strip malls for potential stores to rob, I’m eyeballing side streets for run-down homes in need of a fresh coat of paint or a replacement screen door. Sure, I’m still having an amazing time stealing unique cars and searching for moonlit monsters with a flashlight in flooded swampland areas but, even as I indulge in each incredible new gameplay surprise and jaw-dropping action set piece that GTA 6 serves up, a part of me still wishes I could take an occasional break to paint fences and sand decks like I’m subtly being taught the basics of karate by an aging Japanese gentleman from Okinawa.

pool.titulo: GTA's treatment of women 'has not been good', says Rockstar vet delighted by 'long overdue' female protagonist in GTA 6
pool.resumen: Lucia has stans everywhere.
pool.contenido:
Lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.
That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens , GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue".
Baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built".
That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".
Baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an important series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist. I think it's been long, long overdue, and I can't wait to get to grips with the game and see how in-depth it goes.
"I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland".

pool.titulo: Queen's Domain review
pool.resumen:
Where to start with Queen's Domain? It's tempting to begin with King's Field; after all, FromSoftware's seminal first-person action-RPG is an explicit inspiration for developer Freshly Baked Games. But 40 hours later, it feels like so much more. It's equally tempting to invoke another FromSoftware game: Dark Souls. Queen's Domain owes an obvious debt to that game's celebrated level design: the dazzling interconnectedness of its vertiginous world. But that's not quite right either. The deeper you delve, the more there's something of the spirit of The Legend of Zelda, a touch of Metroidvania too. Until finally you concede that Queen's Domain, with its remarkable world of densely packed secrets, is very much its own.

pool.titulo: "Abandonaremos Unreal Engine para siempre". Epic Games ha tomado una decisión tan polémica que algunos estudios ya quieren marcharse
pool.resumen:
Epic Games lleva años trabajando para convertir Unreal Engine en una herramienta cada vez más accesible, pero sus planes para la próxima generación del motor gráfico han dado un giro que muy pocos esperaban. Si bien Unreal Engine 6 aún no ha salido al mercado y no se prevé su llegada hasta 2027, la compañía de Tim Sweeney ha anunciado que prescindirá de Blueprints , uno de sus sistemas de programación más populares, desde el mismo día en que llegue al mercado. Una decisión que no solo supone un cambio importante respecto a lo anunciado hace meses, sino que responde a una apuesta cada vez mayor por la inteligencia artificial .
Para entender la importancia de esta decisión, hay que explicar qué es exactamente Blueprints. Hablamos de un sistema de programación visual basado en nodos que permite crear mecánicas, comportamientos e interacciones sin escribir líneas de código. pool.titulo: Should you choose the cut or pure drugs in GTA 6?
pool.resumen: Sell the baby powder-spliced product or real deal in the Dealer's Choice mission.
pool.contenido:
Deciding whether to take the cut or pure drugs in GTA 6 is a decision you'll make during the Dealer's Choice mission in Chapter 3.
The proposal is that if you can pass off the drugs cut with baby powder, you can keep the profit, but the deal might go south if they realise, while bringing the pure stuff should make the dealers happy. Here's what happens if you choose either:
Cut drugs : If you choose the cut drugs, the dealers will immediately realise the stuff is cut with baby powder. They'll confront you, at which point you can either offer to give them half off (which reduces your profit to the same as it would have been if you'd taken pure), or you can tell them to take it or leave it. This second option will cause a gunfight, but assuming you survive, you can grab the money from their car and make maximum profit. This also doesn't have any other consequences. Pure drugs : If you choose this option, you'll make less money, but the deal will go off without a hitch after they test it. That means no gunfights. With that in mind, I'd say the cut drugs are the best to pick. You get maximum profit, a cool shootout that makes the mission less boring, and it doesn't have any significant consequences afterwards.

pool.titulo: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Nvidia CEO: 'I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment'
pool.resumen: That was quick.
pool.contenido:
Nvidia has reinstated its disgraced former CEO and leather jacket collector Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and director of its board, according to a press release today.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia back in 1993, was forced to resign from his positions at the company earlier this month, after it came to light he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean tech firm Megaspeed International who was suspected by US intelligence of being an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security. Huang also admitted to carrying out two additional affairs with Nvidia employees.
He was replaced by Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The Nvidia board initially responded to pressure from tech industry leaders to bring Huang back with a statement that he would not be reinstated . He has now been reinstated.
"Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board", confirmed the corporation in a press release. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.
"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk". Huang has a close relationship with US president Donald Trump, and Trump has backed calls for Huang's reinstatement .
Markets were unhappy with Huang's dismissal earlier this month; when it was announced, Nvidia shed billions of dollars in market value as traders adjusted to the prospect of a future without his leadership. The announcement of his reinstatement has sent Nvidia share prices skyrocketing by over 30%.
"I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution", said Huang. Meanwhile, Nvidia has formed "a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate" Huang's affair with a possible Chinese intelligence asset and says that "investigation will proceed to conclusion.
"Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it".

pool.titulo: Dragon Age's former boss explains that poor management from EA led to BioWare shutting down because 'the options on the table were all terrible'
pool.resumen: "Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something."
pool.contenido:
Mass Effect , Dragon Age , and classics like Neverwinter Nights , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , and the OG Baldur's Gate was being shut down .
The decision was made by EA, just a year after it was acquired by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners (owned by the son-in-law of US president Donald Trump, Jared Kushner).
The reasons? Underperforming games. Dragon Age: The Veilguard didn't hit the mark, Andromeda wasn't well received, and Anthem, the live-service shooter, shut its servers down for good earlier this year.
It's a bad string of events for sure, but former Dragon Age boss Mark Darrah doesn't believe that it's all down to BioWare's poor management. The studio was backed into a corner by EA and the pressure to perform.
Decisions like using the Frostbite Engine, "making Dragon Age 2", and "shipping Anthem" were all products of BioWare needing to hit financial targets set out by EA. "They basically said 'Gotta hit your financials, so what are you going to do?' Darrah says. "'Are you going to ship KOTOR a year sooner than you think is going to happen? No. Are you going to pull Mass Effect in a year? No. It was never clear what the consequence of 'no' was, and it still isn't. But it seemed really dire at the time. So you gotta do something, so what are you going to do? Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something."

pool.titulo: 'The System Is Not Good Vs. Evil': Why GTA 6's Criminal Profile Mechanic Is Dividing Fans
pool.resumen: GTA 6 players are debating the game's Criminal Profile system, and how it operates with more depth than just a straightforward "good vs. evil" morality system.
pool.contenido:
GTA 6 players are debating the game's Criminal Profile scale, and how it operates with more depth than just a straightforward "good vs. evil" morality system.
While previous Rockstar adventures have operated on a simpler, binary scale, GTA 6 offers a more nuanced Criminal Profile that reflects your playstyle — from silent and stealthy to excessively violent and "psycho." But some players have criticised how the gameplay mechanic appears to penalise actions taken in self-defence, while others have suggested it is just not well explained.
From "Professional" all the way to "Irredeemable," GTA 6 tracks each character's actions across a series of five profile labels — and yes, you can make Jason and Lucia have wildly different personalities from each other, depending on your actions as either. But Professional does not mean pacifist, and players will inevitably still rack up a fair body count as they explore more of Leonida — the difference here is how messy you are along the way.
The scale begins with Professional, which reflects actions that align with an undetected or non-lethal play style. Stealth takedowns and non-lethal incapacitations award a focus boost, as do kind acts towards NPCs. Go for limbs (highlighted in yellow while in bullet time) rather than headshots to keep this rating intact, or earn points back towards it if you're currently rated as more wantonly violent.
Next up is Hardened, which reflects a slightly less cautious approach to firefights and taking lives in general. You're headshotting the bad guys rather than incapacitating them, in other words, but not mowing down the innocent cops who try and stop you on the way out.
Turn things up a notch and you get to Violent, where cops and random passers by are being caught up in your rampage. It's at this level that your focus boost switches to pulling off headshots, reflecting your own more violent playstyle. But there's still a way to go yet before you're playing GTA 6 at your worst.
Slip into Pyscho rank and you'll have left a lot of defenceless people and animals smeared across the tarmac or piled up in artfully arranged piles of corpses. It's a this rank that cops are so tired of your bulls**t that the option to surrender gets removed, and probably fair enough.
And then there's Irredeemable. If you don't revert from Psycho after a while — and ignore multiple in-game warnings — you'll permanently slip into Irredeemable territory for the rest of your playthrough. There no way to change your Criminal Profile again and you'll also lose the ability to boost focus, making combat harder. Additionally, there are also story implications — which we won't spoil here.
What seems to be confusing some players is the idea that some killing is accepted by the game even at the game's lowest Criminal Profile ranks, though this appears to be contextual. Headshot a gang member in a hideout after shooting most enemies in the knees and you're unlikely to be seen as too naughty. But fight back against an NPC on the street, or fire at a bank teller rather than simply intimidating them, and the game will take notice.
"The idea of violent vs. professional criminal sounded awesome on paper, but the fact it punishes you for literal SELF-DEFENSE just because you go for headshots is ridiculous to me," wrote content creator Synth Potato in a widely-shared post on X/Twitter. "Carjacking being considered a bad action is also just not thought out enough. By definition it is not a violent crime if no one got hurt, so carjacking is not one. Red Dead 2 did this way better, it made way more sense what is an evil action and what isn't."
"It's important to realize the system is not 'good vs evil' but 'professional criminal vs psychopath,'" countered one reply from GTA fan The24thFrame . "A professional already has their getaway car prepared. A psycho runs into traffic and forces someone out of their car. In my experience you don't have to be *too* stressed about it," they continued. "I have been maintaining 'professional' without issue and I still probably kill about 25% of the enemies. Especially in the more action-heavy missions."
"This," agreed another fan, the appropriately named SirSnipeyy . "I'm profesional BECAUSE I park my car around the corner so it's not seen, I shoot limbs on sight if they pull guns or punch them, I pick locks, wipe tapes, turn off alarms, have outfits ready in the trunk, and escape route planned, and a body shop nearby if needed. It's cool."
"It's a 'Michael to Trevor' scale tbh," wrote wildstar33 , summing up the Character Profile mechanic in a nutshell.
Still, others have said this is not how they played GTA in the past, and prefer the series' previous ability to cause widespread mayhem without consequence. Of course, you can still do that if that's how you want to play the game — but in a story that attempts some level of realism in its character relationships and overall narrative arc, Character Profiles seemingly feel like an attempt at keeping the game grounded.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 Has Given Carly Rae Jepsen's Most Underrated Song Another Shot in the Charts
pool.resumen: GTA 6 has propelled an underrated hit from Carly Rae Jepsen back into the charts for the first time in more than a decade.
pool.contenido:
GTA 6 has propelled an underrated hit from Carly Rae Jepsen back into the charts for the first time in more than a decade.
'Run Away With Me' by Carly Rae Jepsen is taking places on multiple music charts after being used in one of GTA 6's most memorable missions. The song's inclusion has many realising that we've been sleeping on this banger for years, after it failed to make much of a dent in the music charts when it was released in 2015.
Kicking off the week, 'Run Away With Me' is 84th on the Shazam music charts. It joins many other tracks that feature in GTA 6, such as 'Break Free' by Ariana Grande (feat Zedd) and 'Flower In A Hurricane' by Justice (feat Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard), the latter of which takes the top spot overall.
'Run Away With Me' is also a new entry on the iTunes charts, taking the 140th spot. As expected, it's there alongside plenty of GTA 6 hits, with the game having a clear effect on the music charts.
The track is still a way off its initial release-window peak, as it reached 49 in the U.S. pop charts. However, this was shockingly low for a song that received widespread acclaim at the time, seen as one of the best songs of the year. So, its GTA 6-spike is giving it another chance to shine.
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
You'll hear the song in GTA 6 when you're flicking through the radio, but it also takes centre stage during a Chapter 1 mission, Day Release . This is the first time you play as Lucia after the prologue, and the song runs throughout the entire mission, swelling when you jump on a jet ski to get to a yacht party. The song is essentially our introduction to Vice City, and serves as a celebration of Lucia's freedom and hope for a better future.
Now, with GTA 6 selling incredibly well — making an eye-watering $3.79 billion in its first day — we're seeing that success bleed into other mediums. It helps that Rockstar released an official soundtrack right alongside the game, which we're also seeing on the charts, but tracks that didn't even make it onto the album are still performing well.

pool.titulo: The Last Jedi Director Rian Johnson Finally Addresses Whether He'd Ever Return to Star Wars
pool.resumen: Star Wars: The Last Jedi director Rian Johnson has revealed whether he'd ever return to the galaxy far, far away.
pool.contenido:
Star Wars: The Last Jedi director Rian Johnson has revealed whether he'd ever return to the galaxy far, far away.
Speaking this weekend at the Marrakech Film Festival, Johnson was asked for his thoughts on eventually returning to the Star Wars universe, almost a decade on from his divisive sequel trilogy entry. Perhaps surprisingly, Johnson suggested he was still open to the idea — despite the intense backlash to his movie from some of Star Wars' noisest followers.
"I mean, I love Star Wars more now than I ever have," Johnson began (thanks, Variety ). "And it's exciting to me that there are a lot of different voices now, taking cracks at it.
"In terms of... I'm already writing the next thing I’m gonna do, and it's not a Star Wars thing or a Knives Out thing," Johnson revealed. "Right now, I'm very much enjoying making my own stuff, but if the opportunity presented itself, it's a world I deeply love.
"It's also a group of people I deeply love," he concluded. "[Lucasfilm's new co-president] Dave Filoni I got to know making The Last Jedi, I think he's a wonderful, wonderful guy who really has the spirit of Star Wars in him. All the Lucasfilm folks are awesome."
When The Last Jedi launched in 2017 as the second film in Disney's Star Wars sequel trilogy, it received positive critical reviews before a surge of fan criticism took hold. Johnson later said that he anticipated some of this response, and was proud of having made a film that took some bold narrative steps and did more than simply feed fans what they'd expected. Lucasfilm seemed less proud, however, and ensured that elements of The Last Jedi's story were retconned for its bland trilogy closer Rise of Skywalker, while discussions for a whole new trilogy of films led by Johnson fell off the radar completely.
In the meantime, Johnson has finally found widespread success with his Knives Out movie trilogy, for which he has served as writer, director and co-producer. Former Bond star Daniel Craig has led a starry cast in three murder mystery whodunnits so far, released between 2019 and 2025, with a fourth entry expected down the line.
As for Star Wars, while Johnson appears to be leaving the door open to his return some day, Lucasfilm doesn't appear interested at present. Beyond the upcoming Star Wars: Starfighter, which lands in theaters on May 28, the Star Wars production company is yet to lay out a long term vision for the franchise following its recent leadership changes, various short-lived Disney+ TV projects, and a lengthy slate of movie projects cancelled or stuck in development hell. Not even a big screen outing for The Mandalorian and Grogu this year could turn things around, as the movie set a disappointing record for the franchise's lowest live-action theatrical gross.
Fans expect that Filoni and Lucasfilm will use Star Wars' upcoming 50th anniversary year to map out what's next for the franchise in broader detail over the coming 12 moths. Reports suggest that of everything Lucasfilm has previously announced, the new movie/trilogy written by Dark Phoenix's Simon Kinberg is the one currently moving forward . Whether Filoni will also be involved again with Star Wars anytime soon, however, remains to be seen.

pool.titulo: Anthropic Boss Dario Amodei Reportedly Had a Dystopian Solution for Simulating a Fulfilling Life for People Who Lose Their Jobs to AI: Video Games
pool.resumen: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei reportedly once suggested that video games could be the solution to political strife caused by AI-fueled joblessness.
pool.contenido:
Anthropic boss Dario Amodei reportedly once suggested that video games could be the solution to political strife caused by AI-fueled joblessness.
In a profile of Anthropic’s Dario and Daniela Amodei from the Wall Street Journal , it is reported that when Dario Amodei worked at OpenAI from 2016 to 2020, he allegedly suggested video games could pacify the masses after AI took their jobs.
Here’s the relevant section of the profile:
There [at OpenAI], he engaged in debates with his fellow employees, suggesting that immersive video games might be a solution for the political strife caused by AI-induced joblessness, according to widely circulated Slack messages. The anecdote suggests a foresight from Dario Amodei about the potential of AI to cause mass layoffs, but also a rather dystopian solution that would see jobless people content to live out their lives playing video games rather than kick up a stink about losing their livelihoods.
While this section of the WSJ profile mentioned Amodei’s alleged thoughts on this issue from some time ago (potentially a decade ago), and he may have changed his mind since then, it’s interesting to consider his mindset in the context of growing concern around mass layoffs as companies turn to AI to replace human workers to save money and, they claim, boost productivity.
Survey data from Pew Research Center published in September showed how ordinary people around the world are worried about the economic impact of AI. In 34 of 37 countries Pew Research Center surveyed earlier this year , people tend to believe AI will lead to fewer jobs rather than more jobs. And people are getting more worried about this over time. In the U.S., the share of people who believe AI will result in job loss over the next 20 years increased seven percentage points in two years.
The profile also has a delicious timing, coming as it does around the launch of GTA 6 , a game that you’d imagine Dario Amodei might have considered to be a video game "immersive enough" to pacify the jobless masses long term.
Reaction online to the profile is, predictably, a mix of outrage and mockery, with some posting The Matrix and Ready Player One memes in response. "Unless we’d get paid for playing video games, I don’t see how that would work. Boredom isn’t the problem with joblessness," one person said. “How do people buy games if they don't have a job that pays them?” another wondered.
The answer from people who are convinced of our AI-powered future to that common retort is, as Elon Musk is fond of saying, abundance for all. Musk believes that AI will create a post-scarcity economy where goods and services have become so plentiful that labor and money become redundant. In such an economy, no-one would need a job, because, so the theory goes, everyone has all they could ever want at the push of a button — for free.
In such an economy, could video games keep everyone occupied enough to prevent political strife? Could a game like GTA 6 keep you busy… forever?
Photographer: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

pool.titulo: Avengers: Doomsday Runtime Revealed as Trailer Teased for Today
pool.resumen: Fans are expecting a fresh Avengers: Doomsday trailer today, and now have a good idea of the movie's runtime.
pool.contenido:
Fans are expecting a fresh Avengers: Doomsday trailer today, and now have a good idea of the movie's runtime.
With Marvel's highly-anticipated blockbuster less than a month away, viewers are awaiting a chunky new look at the film after what feels like a long wait. Happily, however, that wait seems to be at its end — according to Peggy Carter actress Hayley Atwell.
"There's a new trailer dropping on Monday... am I allowed to have said that?" Atwell told fans in New York over the weekend while signing autographs, according to Deadline . (We're guessing that no, she probably wasn't allowed to say that.)
If Atwell's intel is correct, this would be our first substantial look at Doomsday in months. Marvel began its rollout of Doomsday teasers last December, when it started launching a series of teasers focused on Steve Rogers, Thor, the X-Men and then the Wakandans plus Fantastic Four. A proper trailer then followed in July, showing our first look at Robert Downey Jr. in character as Doctor Doom. Now, with the movie imminent, fans want more.
Over the past year, Marvel has dropped a few more hints and tidbits, and in the past few weeks fans have got confirmation that Elizabeth Olsen is back in the MCU as her fan-favorite character Scarlet Witch, while Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld has just confirmed her own Doomsday return . (Fans also strongly suspect Ms. Marvel actress Iman Vellani is on the cusp of her own Doomsday confirmation, since she appears to be sitting on the same kind of Doomsday set chair for recent episodes of her official Marvel podcast.)
This year's other MCU releases also featured fresh story beats that connected with Doomsday, with the end of Spider-Man: Brand New Day teasing a Spidey in space, while Avengers: Endgame Encore included looks at what Steve Rogers, the Hulk, and the TVA where up to as Doctor Doom arrives.
"We’ve done a series of tags around the characters because the story actually started [with the Steve Rogers teaser]," Doomsday co-director Joe Russo said during a chat with the Qatar Film Committee. "And you’ve been watching it slowly unfold and these are all pieces of something that are going to equal two and a half hours of your time on December 18," he continued, apparently confirming the movie will run to around 150 minutes.
This would make the film the same length as 2018's similar Avengers movie Infinity War, and shorter than Eternals, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, and the three-hour Avengers: Endgame.
Here's hoping Atwell is correct and we're just hours away from seeing more of what those 150 minutes will contain. Either way, Avengers: Doomsday launches on December 18.

In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

pool.titulo: This fan-made map shows why Queen's Domain is the true GOTY, and you can even upload your save to it to track the things you have left to find
pool.resumen: Cartographic miracles.
pool.contenido:
The world wants me to write more about Grand Theft Auto 6 and I bravely answer "No". Last week, I obtained 50% of the endings available in Queen's Domain, the best videogame to release in the year 2026. The next 50% require, well, a lot of nook-scouring and cranny-uncovering—many more hours of gameplay which I am preserving for myself as a Christmas holiday treat.
And when I do, I suspect I might make a little (just a little) use of this rad Queen's Domain map by a creator called Leny15 . Barely a week ago I wrote that "I suspect a cross-section of [Queen's Domain's] goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art". Well, I was right. Here it is and it looks rad as hell.
No, really. Even if you're not a Queen's Domain player—or maybe especially if you're not—take a look at this thing. It's one thing to wander these maps as a player, it's another to get a totally flexible birdseye view of how dense, twisty and interconnected they are. I will never stop being blown away by how knotty and elaborate this game is; I love it.
I will also never believe I have actually explored all of it. I'll be honest, gang, I really feel like I've plumbed the depths of this game, but this map has entries for areas I ain't even heard of, and even those areas that I have heard of seem to contain secret sub-areas I've barely touched.
My favourite feature of this thing has got to be the ability to upload your save to it, at which point it will give you a completion percentage and tick off the collectibles and secrets you've already attained (reminder that you can download your Steam cloud saves right in your browser). I was heartened to read that I have, it seems, done in about 70% of this game already. I was even more heartened to learn that the remaining 30% seems even stranger, more complicated, and more baffling than all the rest. I can't wait to check it out.

pool.titulo: 60 hours in GTA 6 has me yearning for an online Leonida
pool.resumen: Leonida deserves to be explored with friends.
pool.contenido:
I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6 's Leonida. Rockstar has delivered on its promise of both breadth and depth—the map is huge, but utterly stuffed with detail. Large, open highways shrink into single lanes surrounded by construction that force me to slam the brakes. Sidewalks sparse with pedestrians eventually lead to densely packed retail areas, restaurants, and clubs.
Pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction. You don't need to undertake any missions in these areas to understand the people that live here—Rockstar has nailed so much of the environmental storytelling and the conversations between NPCs you'll stumble on as you roam.
It's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting. I spent an ungodly amount of time in GTA 5's Online mode when it first released. I was there on the ground for its incredibly shaky launch (I made a character and then got stuck in that birdseye view loading screen for hours, incredible stuff) and continued to sink time into it over the years, particularly during Covid.
And I like it well enough, but its novelty has waned over the last decade. Its core experience is inherently different from what singleplayer brings, and I had yearned to return to a world less about blowing other players up with flying motorbikes and more about, well, blowing non-players up with regular motorbikes.
But after 60 hours roaming around Leonida and witnessing what it has to offer? I now want nothing more than for Rockstar to spin this map into the next generation of Online. Even outside of missions and driving around, there are so many little things that I would kill to do with pals.
Grab a pack of brewskis from the convenience store, hop in a boat, and go fishing. Throw on our best all-American attire and get down and dirty in some mud racing. Seek out other players meticulously planning a jewellery store hold-up, only to swoop in and steal the goods for ourselves. Hit up the gym for a little workout before nipping to a nearby restaurant for a bite to eat. Leonida is a place that is so rife with things to do, and I can imagine doing almost all of them with some buddies by my side.
It's also the perfect opportunity for Rockstar to introduce things that are sorely missing for me right now. A lack of safehouses makes sense with GTA 6's offline story, but I yearn to buy highrise apartments and suburban houses. Maybe even buy a business or two, for a little side cash. There's also the matter of that gigantic casino and the go-kart track that are currently inaccessible but the latter of which is donning a large "COMING SOON" sign. It feels like I'm being taunted. Surely you wouldn't put these things in the game with no intention of opening them at some point… right?
And even as someone who was never interested in nor dabbled with GTA Online's flourishing roleplaying scene, I've encountered so many instances where I've thought roleplaying in Leonida actually be pretty darn neat. I could become a RydeMe driver, or a Snapmatic influencer, or a backwater recluse who lives off the land. And when the game comes to PC? The potential for bending the world to account for even more professions becomes all the greater.
Rockstar hasn't actually said a damn thing about GTA 6 Online right now, but it feels inevitable. Leonida is the biggest playground the developer has given players to date, and unleashing players across its sprawling map is Online's natural evolution. And, y'know, considering how much money GTAO has made over the last 13 years, I'm almost certain that Rockstar won't leave that kind of opportunity on the table.

pool.titulo: World of Warcraft: Forever review: The first proper MMO adventure I've been on in years
pool.resumen: A second wind for old-school MMOs that has me hooked.
pool.contenido:
World of Warcraft: Forever has, much as the original World of Warcraft did back in 2004, completely consumed my life. I write about games for a living, mind, so the attention vortex it has wrought upon me is primarily professional obligation, rather than just irresponsibility.
Need to know What is it?: A reimagining of 2004's World of Warcraft, with new balancing, lighting, dungeons, and items.
Expect to pay: A monthly subscription of $14.99/£10.99. Optional race and early-game zone behind a £25.99/$30 paywall.
Developer: Blizzard Entertainment
Publisher: Blizzard Entertainment
Reviewed on: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, AMD Ryzen 7 5800 8-Core Processor, 16GB RAM, Force MP600 SSD
Multiplayer?: Yes
Link: Official site
But at the time of writing, it has been 443 hours since Forever's launch. I have spent 147 of those hours asleep (less, but let's just pretend I've been getting a solid eight), leaving around 296 hours of my waking mind. 230 of them have been spent playing World of Warcraft.
That's a deeply concerning amount of time if I wasn't getting a salary to review it—it has been part of my 9-5. I've also often been keeping the game open while I, you know, feed and bathe myself and do chores. So we're probably just in the realm of 'moderately worrying' rather than 'cause for a wellness check'.
Don't worry, I intend to take a break soon: But during those 230 hours, I have hit level 60, entered 31 dungeons, completed 941 quests, levelled engineering, mining, and first aid to 300, and apparently /waved at other players 50 times. Which are rookie numbers that I need to get up.
But I've also found myself taking in the scenery, laughing at my poor luck at bottles, whining about the drop rates of basilisk brains, splitting mining nodes with party members, mercilessly grinding ogres into paste for my first mount, and talking to more strangers while questing than I have in years of playing more modern, streamlined MMOs.
I'm not pointing this out to simply cast aside the role of nostalgia in my enjoyment, but I do think nostalgia can only carry an attention span so far. It certainly doesn't keep 230 hours of medically inadvisable gameplay afloat on its own. There's something else going on here; something special that's been unearthed.
All of the things that made an old-school MMO like the original WoW so deeply enthralling back in 2004 are not simply dated, to be cast aside as an inferior form of videogame.
The crappy drop rates, the fighting over tags, the running everywhere (there is so much running everywhere) while not always justified, is part of an experience that's stronger for its inconveniences. The friction burn you get from jutting up against a game that's occasionally just hostile to you. All of that connects you to the world, and the people in it, in a very real way.
Back with the old, in with the new First, I want to talk about what Forever itself has actually brought to the table. After all, much of what I've talked about already has been reverence paid to a series of design decisions that were made over 20 years ago.
In the here and now, though, Forever has around 1,000 new quests (the original WoW is estimated to've had somewhere in the mid-2,000s, so that's approximately 30-50% more Warcraft), nine new dungeons, and two new major levelling zones in Mount Hyjal and The Riverglades.
To encourage and support levelling alts, Blizzard's added a new mechanic in the Legacy tree—a genuinely cool feature that encourages you to level alts (or do endgame achievements and raids) to unlock perks, like making levelling slightly easier by giving you a small heal when you kill an enemy in the open world, or by giving you more resources when you gather things.
Then there's the retooled class and item balance, the latter of which is my one, very mild point of disappointment: There's an increasing amount of trinkets and weapons I've kept around for specific use cases, sure, but at least while levelling, the fantasy of equipping an anti-worgen sword to do some worgen-killing quests (as so often quoted in Blizzard's promotional material) hasn't quite panned out. That's not to say it's gone by the wayside completely, though.
I've seen a two-handed axe that lets you get mining nodes, a knife that lets you skin humanoids, gloves that increase your mining skill, boots that let you walk under water, and so on. It's just not a core part of the levelling experience.
It does also improve somewhat when you get into the later levels. For instance, I now have a two-handed questing sword green that I'll keep in my bags basically forever because it lets me spin around like a propeller to slow my fall speed: And I'm a Warrior, so that's a hugely useful traversal tool for someone without any way to slow fall.
Professions have also had a total facelift, and for the first time, I'm actually levelling crafting and gathering skills on my characters because of it.
Not only do crafting ones like blacksmithing actually give you really good gear as you level up (rather than just a couple of big capstone items) but all professions can now turn in writs and crates, buying new recipes via the latter and unlocking them with a rep grind via the former.
The new zones are both excellent—the Riverglades is pretty, but not out of place, whereas Hyjal is a satisfying (and very efficient) climb up a mythological mountain ruined by war, with some legitimately cool questlines to it. In both, questing is enough of a breeze that it does feel almost too easy, with Hyjal smoothing over the typically arduous 58-60 grind completely. But they're not any more efficient than, say, The Burning Crusade's better zones, which is a level of kayfabe-breaking I can get behind.
A light touch But until you hit that point, Forever's newness is downright subtle. A chain here, a few fetch quests there. Just enough to make questing in every zone worth it, just enough to even out the occasional, clunky speedbumps.
